doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 102806 - EM_XG2_PSX_BOOT_FAILURE_PRI
body:
ERROR: EM_XG2_PSX_BOOT_FAILURE_PRI
Protected image startup of the XG2 (XPS-PC2 X axis) failed. Check EMO reset and perform a TPS reset. If this error occurs again, contact your service representative.
Extended error: The XPS-PC2 inside X axis XPS failed to boot into protected mode.
* Verify that the X axis XPS and entire XG2 gradient subsystem is powered on.
* Verify that emergency stop is not active.
* Verify that the X axis dual-fiber cable is connected and properly seated into the IXG SFP transceiver module and X axis XPS.
* Verify X axis dual fiber optic cable linkup status and that there are no communication faults pertaining to the SFP transceiver modules in X axis XPS or in corresponding communications port on IXG board. SFP modules can be swapped between units for troubleshooting.
* Verify that both ends of the X axis XPS SFP Fiber cable are not damaged.
* Check the X axis XPS Heartbeat LED from the front panel is blinking.
* If Heartbeat LED not blinking then check condition of PDU 48V PS2 power supply.
* Power down the XG2 subsystem and reseat cables to X axis XPS. If these steps do not resolve the problem, replace the X axis XPS and perform a TPS reset.

Extended error: Ensure the Octavius2 cable is not damaged and is properly connected between the XPS and XGA and reseat the cable. To verify cable is working properly, swap Octavius cables and perform a TPS reset (Note: swapping the cable will change the axis ID of the module). If the fault continues to be reported on the same axis ID after a TPS reset, replace the Ocativus cable. If the fault is reported on a new axis ID after a TPS reset, replace the XPS with the Ocativus cable ID reporting the issue.

title: 102827 - EM_XG2_AC2_LINK_DOWN
body:
ERROR: EM_XG2_AC2_LINK_DOWN
The %b XGA is reporting an Axis Link Down Fault.
Extended error: Check the dual-fiber optic cable on both the IXG and XGA sides to ensure a proper connection, reseat the SFP modules and cables and perform a TPS reset. If error persists, swap the XGA dual-fiber optic cable with another XGA dual-fiber optic cable at the IXG and perform a TPS reset. If the fault is now reported on a different axis ID, See IXG Troubleshooting. If the fault is reported on the same axis ID, see XGA Troubleshooting. *XGA Troubleshooting: Swap SFP modules between two XGAs and perform a TPS reset. If the error is reported on a new axis, replace the failing SFP module, if the error is reported on the same the same axis ID, swap dual-fiber optic cables on both ends of the link and perform a TPS reset. If the error is reported on a new axis, replace the cable, if the error is reported on the same axis replace the XGA. *IXG Troubleshooting: Swap the SFP module of the failing axis with another SFP module at the IXG and perform a TPS reset. If the error is reported on a new axis, replace the failing SFP. If the error is being reported on the same axis, replace the IXG.

title: 102964 - EM_XG2_AXIS2G_LINK_DOWN_ON_SINGLE_AXIS
body:

The PC2 and AC2 %b Axis2G links are down on a single axis.
Extended error: Check the Axis2G link LEDs on the IXG. If fault LEDs are displayed for both the XPS and XGA of the same axis, check the 48V power on the XPS and XGA by checking the front panel LEDs. If all LEDs are off, there is no power to the XPS and XGA. If the XPS and XGA have no power, check that the 48V power cable is connected from the PDU to the XPS and from the XPS to the XGA. If the front panel LEDs of the XPS and XGA are lit, check the dual-fiber cables and SFP modules at the XPS/XGA and the IXG. Dual-fiber cables and transceiver modules may be swapped to try and isolate the failure.

Run the APS, AGP, and SCP Host Data path ping tests to check the Ethernet connections. Run the APS, AGP, and SCP Board Level Diagnostics to check the SCSI Serial Expansion. The STIF Board serial connection is not tested. If both sets of diagnostics pass but yet the TPS Reset still fails then please closely inspect the serial connection between the SCSI Serial Expansion and the MGD STIF Board.

body:
ERROR: EM_mrNSP_VRE_RESET_FAILED
Failed to reset the VRE. Please perform a System Restart.
Extended error: This is the most generic error message for VRE reset failures. It should never occur and could point to flaws in the VRE reset code portion within the NSP. A System Restart may be required in that case.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)

Extended error: During TPS Reset we also reset the VRE (and all its ICNs). This failure means that we could not recover all the ICNs and will have to run with a reduced configuration (fail over mode). The customer can keep scanning but the faulty ICN(s) should be replaced as quickly as possible to restore full recon performance.

body:

Extended error: Before the recon servers can be launched on the VRE an MPI network of processes has to be established (for parallel processing support). Getting this message indicates that the VRE reset scripts were unable to launch that process on the host machine. A System Restart should fix this problem.

Getting this message indicates that the VRE reset scripts were unable to launch that process on the machine specified. The MAC address of each ICN is printed on a label located on the back of the ICN. A System Restart should fix this problem.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2223863 - EM_mrNSP_VRE_RESET_MPI_STARTUP_FAILURE
body:
ERROR: EM_mrNSP_VRE_RESET_MPI_STARTUP_FAILURE
MPI network startup failed. Please perform System Restart.
Extended error: Before the recon servers can be launched on the VRE a MPI network of processes has to be established (for parallel processing support). Getting this message means that we did not encounter an error during the MPI startup sequence but detected that the network wasn't running in the end. There can be many reasons for this to occur such as network problems, faulty ICNs etc.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2223864 - EM_mrNSP_VRE_RESET_CANNOT_COPY_BINARY
body:
ERROR: EM_mrNSP_VRE_RESET_CANNOT_COPY_BINARY
An executable file necessary to run image reconstruction cannot be copied (path %s).
Extended error: During TPS Reset the VRE ICNs will attempt to somtimes copy binary executables from the host. If this fails it is possible that those executables have been deleted or a network or NFS problem is preventing the ICN to pull the file from the host. It is also possible that the executable is still running on the machine and can therefore not be overridden. If this problem presists a software reload may be required.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2223865 - EM_mrNSP_VRE_RESET_ATTEMPTING_RECOVERY
body:
ERROR: EM_mrNSP_VRE_RESET_ATTEMPTING_RECOVERY
Unable to reset VRE, will try to recover before failing TPS Reset.
Extended error: Internally the VRE reset code has the ability to detect problems and attempt to correct them. This usually means rebooting the VRE. Other operator level messages are logged to inform the operator that the TPS Reset will take longer than normal.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2223866 - EM_mrNSP_VRE_RESET_FAILED_AFTER_RECOVERY_NO_FAILOVER
body:
ERROR: EM_mrNSP_VRE_RESET_FAILED_AFTER_RECOVERY_NO_FAILOVER
Failed to reset the VRE. All attempts to recover have failed. Try performing a System Restart and call Service on repeated occurrence.
Extended error: During TPS Reset we also reset the VRE (and all its ICNs). This failure means that we could not recover the VRE. Scanning won't be possible. Most likely there is a problem with one or more ICNs and their connection to the host. Seeing this message also means that fail-over (i.e. running the VRE with a reduced set of ICNs) wasn't possible. A host reboot may potentially fix this problem. Troubleshoot VRE subsystem.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)

The TPS Reset has failed because the VRE could not be reset properly. Do you want the system to attempt to recover by running the VRE in degraded mode? This will affect image reconstruction performance negatively.
Extended error: This message is displayed to the operator in form of a popup during after the VRE failed to reset during a TPS reset. He can select OK to accept or CANCEL to decline and try another TPS Reset.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2223869 - EM_mrNSP_VRE_PROMPT_OPERATOR_FOR_CONFIG_CHANGE_COMMMIT
body:
ERROR: EM_mrNSP_VRE_PROMPT_OPERATOR_FOR_CONFIG_CHANGE_COMMMIT
VRE configuration changes detected. Do you want the system to accept these changes? Selecting OK means that the VRE will potentially run in degraded mode (which reduces image reconstruction performance) and the System needs to be restarted.
Extended error: This message is displayed to the operator in form of a popup at the beginning on the TPS Reset. Seeing this means that the VRE configuration has been changed, which could mean that ICNs were disabled, enabled, added, removed etc. A System Restart will be necessary for those changes to take affect, therefore the current TPS Reset will fail if OK is selected. Selecting CANCEL will undo all VRE configuration changes and attempt to reset with the current configuration.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2223870 - EM_mrNSP_VRE_BAD_CONFIG_CHANGE_ADVISORY
body:
ERROR: EM_mrNSP_VRE_BAD_CONFIG_CHANGE_ADVISORY
VRE configuration changes detected. Cannot accept the current VRE configuration changes as image reconstruction could no longer be performed. The current TPS Reset will fail, please notify Service.
Extended error: This message is displayed to the operator in form of a popup at the beginning or end of the TPS Reset. Seeing this means that the VRE configuration has been changed but in a way that makes it impossible to scan. This could happen either because there are no ICNs left in the configuration or because those ICNs left are missing features necessary for scanning, such as acquisition hardware or Infiniband connections.

Extended error: This message is displayed to the operator in form of a popup during a TPS Reset to remind him that we're running the VRE in degraded mode. This means that one or more ICNs have been disabled either because they caused TPS Reset failures and thus were removed automatically or because they were disabled manually by Service. The customer can keep scanning but the faulty ICN(s) should be replaced as quickly as possible to restore full recon performance.

title: 2223880 - EM_mrNSP_RESET_FAILED_BOARD_STATUS
body:
ERROR: EM_mrNSP_RESET_FAILED_BOARD_STATUS
Reset TPS was not successful. Board Failure Status: APS: %s,
SCP: %s,
AGP: %s,
VRE: %s.
ErrorNo: %d.
Extended error: The MGD failed to start a TPS Reset. Either the serial connection to the MGD STIF Board is not working or the Ethernet connection from the Host to the MGD Hub is not working. Run the APS, AGP, and SCP Host Data path ping tests to check the Ethernet connections. Run the APS, AGP, and SCP Board Level Diagnostics to check the SCSI Serial Expansion. The STIF Board serial connection is not tested. If both sets of diagnostics pass but yet the TPS Reset still fails then please closely inspect the serial connection between the SCSI Serial Expansion and the MGD STIF Board. APS, AGP, and SCP Board Level Diagnostics included. VRE failure can sometimes trigger the failure of MGD boards. Failure of SCP with APS/AGP board can be a indicator on the failure on respective board. On APS,SCP,AGP failure run the Board Level Diagnostics to conform the status.

title: 2223881 - EM_mrNSP_TPS_RESET_COMMCTN_TIMED_OUT

TPS Reset Communication Failure:
Host to %s board ethernet communication timed out during TPS Reset.
Extended error: Verify the following to determine the cause of this failure:
Check that the MGD Chassis is turned on and power supplies are OK.
Check that the board is properly seated, there are no bent pins on the backplane slot for the board, and the board has power.
Check that the ethernet connection to the board is present.
Check that the term server to STIF board reset cable connection is good and that the term server power and ethernet connection is good.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2224842 - EM_SRI_SERVO_FAILURE
body:
ERROR: EM_SRI_SERVO_FAILURE
Table motion was stopped because it moved differently than expected. This can occur if the table was moved by hand.
Last Velocity Commanded: %c%d mm/sec
Measured Cradle Velocity: %c%d mm/sec
Extended error: The SRI detected that the cradle moved at a velocity different than what was commanded. This message is expected to be logged when the operator moves the cradle by hand.
Do not troubleshoot based on this error alone. This issue should only be investigated if the site reports the cradle stopping before it gets to the desired position along with this message being logged.
To investigate, run the table motion diagnostic.
If the commanded and measured velocity are both in the same direction (both positive or both negative) and the measured velocity is less than the expected velocity, then there could be a table obstruction preventing the cradle from moving fast enough. Check the cradle and trolley for friction points to the table and bridge. Make sure the belt has proper motion.
If the previous checks pass, make sure that the encoder shielding is intact and that the encoder to SRI cable shielding is intact. If the encoder is OK, check the long drive motor, the SSM or PHPS, and the SRI.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: Encoder, Long Drive Motor, Long Drive Amp, SSM, PHPS, SRI

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2224864 - EM_SRI_SAFETY_VELOCITY
body:
ERROR: EM_SRI_SAFETY_VELOCITY
Table motion was stopped because it was moving faster than expected. This can occur if the table was moved by hand.
Limit: 150 mm/sec
Last Velocity Commanded: %c%d mm/sec
Measured Cradle Velocity: %c%d mm/sec
Extended error: The SRI detected that the cradle was moving faster than the high velocity limit indicated in the message. This message is expected to be logged when the operator moves the cradle by hand.
Do not troubleshoot based on this error alone. This issue should only be investigated if the site reports the cradle coming to a sudden stop or jerky motion during a move along with this message being logged.
To investigate, run the table motion diagnostic. Make sure that the encoder shielding is intact and that the encoder to SRI cable shielding is intact. If the encoder is OK, check the long drive motor, the SSM or PHPS, and the SRI.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: Encoder, Long Drive Motor, Long Drive Amp, SSM, PHPS, SRI

title: 2238402 - EM_GAP_AMP_CLK_STOP
body:
ERROR: EM_GAP_AMP_CLK_STOP
Hardware Error - No Gradient Clock.\b\ A gradient clock stop occurred. The GAP stopped receiving the gradient clock from the IPG. Check the connection between the TYME Board and the GAP Board, then run fiber optic diagnostics.
Extended error: This error condition can also be caused by the Gradient Data Clock Fiber Optic Cables or HSSD Cables being located in the wrong position . In addition to generating this error, if the Gradient Data Clock is not correctly connected, then the system will not go Ready either. Also, if this error seems to be intermittent, and you are getting many other errors, and you have been Resetting TPS, or running Gradient Driver Tests, then, it is possible that IPG could not report all of the tests that have been generated. If this is the case, check the Gradient Data Cable connections to ensure that all, including the Gradient Clock, are in the correct location. When the errors come back from these tests, then check the last line in the error message that reads Low: XXXv High: XXXv Value: 0V axis: XXXXXXX" Notice that if all the error messages that read values are coming back with a value of 0v, or 0mV, then this is an indication the Gradient Clock may be missing.This could also indicate a power problem somewhere in this subsystem. check for things that are common to the axis that are failing."

title: 2238410 - EM_GAP_AMP_X_H_OVERLOAD
body:
ERROR: EM_GAP_AMP_X_H_OVERLOAD
X Axis Gradient Overload Occurred.\b\ The X axis HIGH 8645 Power Module has reported an overload. An overload is the result of the power module output voltage not following the input command.
Extended error: To make sure that you are not looking at faulty sensing from the ASM Board, try swapping the ASM Board for the axis with the fault with an ASM Board from another axis to see if the problem changes axis. If the problem changes axis, then the ASM Board is bad. Remember to use proper ESD practices when changing these boards. If the ASM's are OK, and this is a system with a GRAM, then there is probably a GRAM current distortion error and/or an analog saturation error. If this error occurs during GRAM Tuning, then the VBUS (Bus Voltage Regulator) may not be set up correctly.(This calibration is in the GRAM Tuning procedure.) Adjust this parameter per the GRAM Tuning Calibration, and try again.

title: 2238544 - EM_GAP_RTM_IOUT_H_ERROR
body:
ERROR: EM_GAP_RTM_IOUT_H_ERROR
ASM IOUT_H Monitoring Error. Output Current on HIGH 8645 Power Module has exceeded the maximum range allowed.
Low: %6da High: %6da Value: %6da axis: %c Standby/Ready State: %c
Extended error: To make sure that you are not looking at faulty sensing from the ASM Board, try swapping the ASM Board for the axis with the fault with an ASM Board from another axis to see if the problem changes axis. If the problem changes axis, then the ASM Board is bad. Remember to use proper ESD practices when changing these boards This error condition can also be caused by the Gradient HSSD Cables being located in the wrong position. In addition to generating this error, if the Gradient Data Clock is not correctly connected, then the system will not go Ready. One way to check the Gradient Data Clock connections is to check the last line of the error messages. If it reads Low: XXXv High: XXXv Value: 0V axis: XXXXXXX", then this is an indication the Gradient Clock may be missing. This could also indicate a power problem somewhere in the subsystem. Check for things that are common to the axes that are failing."

For details on troubleshooting this Gradient Bits problem, use the functional block diagrams to trace the gradient bits data path.

It is critical to use this filtered outlet because noise from other sources of power can feed from the scope back into the GRAM Control Board causing calibrations and measurements to be extremely inaccurate. If your oscilloscope uses a voltage other than the 120VAC from the Service Outlet, then try using a step up transformer plugged into this filtered service outlet. doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2238744 - EM_GAP_GRTM_V_BUS_0_ERROR
body:
ERROR: EM_GAP_GRTM_V_BUS_0_ERROR
GASM V_BUS +HI Monitoring Error. The GRAM VBUS +HI voltage is not within the allowed range.
Low: %6dv High: %6dv Value: %6dv axis: %c Standby/Ready State: %c
Extended error: To make sure that you are not looking at faulty sensing from the GASM Board, try swapping the GASM Board for the axis with the fault with an GASM Board from another axis to see if the problem changes axis. If the problem changes axis, then the GASM Board is bad. Remember to use proper ESD practices when changing these boards. This error condition can also be caused by the Gradient HSSD Cables being located in the wrong position. In addition to generating this error, if the Gradient Data Clock is not correctly connected, then the system will not go Ready. One way to check the Gradient Data Clock connections is to check the last line of the error messages. If it reads Low: XXXv High: XXXv Value: 0V axis: XXXXXXX", then this is an indication the Gradient Clock may be missing. This could also indicate a power problem somewhere in the subsystem. Check for things that are common to the axes that are failing."

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2238800 - EM_GAP_X_GRAM_CONFIG_ERROR
body:
ERROR: EM_GAP_X_GRAM_CONFIG_ERROR
GRADIENT CONFIGURATION ERROR.\b\ The MRconfig.cfg file indicates a X axis GRAM is present, but the DIP switch on the front of the MIF is not set. The GAP software is not controlling the GRAM, but analog Vin and voltage control are set in GRAM mode.
Extended error: If the MRConfig.cfg file has been changed, a Reset TPS MUST be performed. After a Reset TPS, SPI will check the MRconfig.cfg file to compare the software configuration of with the hardware settings. If the hardware differs from the MRconfig.cfg file, SPI will log an error, and will not allow the Gradient Driver Subsystem to go Ready. Swap the ASM Board for the axis with the fault with an ASM Board from another axis to see if the problem changes axis. If the problem changes axis, then the ASM Board is bad. If the problem stays on the same axis, try swapping the GASM Board for the axis with the fault with a GASM Board from another axis to see if the problem changes axis. If the problem changes axis, then the GASM Board is bad. Remember to use proper ESD practices when changing these boards.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2239176 - EM_GDT_REG_GRAM_POWER_OFF
body:
ERROR: EM_GDT_REG_GRAM_POWER_OFF
GRADIENT DRIVER TESTS - Power Up GRAM %c Axis Register Pattern Test Failed. Power appears to be off. Possible causes: GRAM Power Supply, cable between GAP & GRAM, GRAM control board, GAP board, or the MIF DIP switch is set improperly.
Extended error: Verify that the front MIF DIP switch that is marked 'GRAM' is set properly. This DIP switch defines if a GRAM is present or if a GRAM is not present. doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2239207 - EM_GDT_LOC_ASM_AGND_RANGE
body:
ERROR: EM_GDT_LOC_ASM_AGND_RANGE
GRADIENT DRIVER TESTS - ASM %c Axis AGND voltage out of range. Re-seat the ASM, if problem persists swap ASM. If problem moves, replace ASM, else replace MIF.
Low: %10.3fV High: %10.3fV Value: %10.3fV
Extended error: To make sure that you are not looking at faulty sensing from the ASM Board, try swapping the ASM Board for the axis with the fault with an ASM Board from another axis to see if the problem changes axis. If the problem changes axis, then the ASM Board is bad. Remember to use proper ESD practices when changing these boards. This error condition can also be caused by the Gradient HSSD Cables being located in the wrong position. In addition to generating this error, if the Gradient Data Clock is not correctly connected, then the system will not go Ready. One way to check the Gradient Data Clock connections is to check the last line of the error messages. If it reads Low: XXXv High: XXXv Value: 0V axis: XXXXXXX", then this is an indication the Gradient Clock may be missing. This could also indicate a power problem somewhere in the subsystem. Check for things that are common to the axes that are failing."

GRADIENT DRIVER TESTS - Static Test MIF %c Axis Configuration Error. Required: Current Sum=0, Low-side Invert=1, Serv Mode=0, Manual Ena=0. Current: Current Sum=%d, Low-side Invert=%d, Serv Mode=%d, Manual Ena=%d. No tests will be run on this axis.
Extended error: Current Sum configuration error could cause this fault. Move the DIP switch (S1) on the MIF Circuit Board to the Current Sum true position. Low side inverter configuration error could also cause this fault. Move the DIP switch (S2) on the MIF Circuit Board to the Low Side Polarity true position. Service mode is the logic OR of switches S4-1 through S4-5 (these are the DIP switches on the MIF front panel)...the first five dip switches must be set in the up configuration. Your system should not be in the Manual Enable mode...it must be in GAP control...S3, the three position slide switch should be all the way to the right (series switch can be down) After a Reset TPS, SPI will check the MRconfig.cfg file to compare the software configuration of with the hardware settings. If the hardware differs from the MRconfig.cfg file, SPI will log an error, and will not allow the Gradient Driver Subsystem to go Ready. If all switches are correct, and the problem still exists, then swap the MIF chassis of the axis with the fault with a MIF chassis of another axis, and re-run this test.

Extended error: If the system is a Signa Horizon, there would be no current output. The image would look like a flat image. If the system has a GRAM, then an error message would have indicated a fault, and the scanner would not be permitted to go to Ready. If there was a G in the ipg_stage file, and you performed a scan, the output voltage would be proportional to the DAC signal. This will generate too much voltage and an I Overcurrent and I Distorition fault will occur. If too much current is generated, then there will be an overload condition. In either case, replace the MIF Module.

title: 2239279 - EM_GDT_STAT_LOW_PM_CFG
body:
ERROR: EM_GDT_STAT_LOW_PM_CFG
GRADIENT DRIVER TESTS - %b Tests %c Axis Low Power Module Config Error. The DUAL DIP switch on the MIF is set, but software does not detect a Low Power Module. To test this axis, check power, fuses, and cables to Low Module and run test again.
Extended error: The DIP switch indicates that the system is either a Signa Horizon or a Signa Horizon EchoSpeed. If this system is a Signa Horizon HiSpeed, then this dip switch needs to be changed to indicate a single Power Module per axis. If the DIP switch is set, then the MIF is not reading it. 0It is possible that the MIF Module is not functioning properly. Swap the MIF Module for the failed axis with a MIF Module for a working axis, and run the test again. If the problem moved, then the MIF Module for the failed axis needs to be replaced. Other possible causes are the Main Board or cables from the MIF to the Main Board. To isolate further, check for power to the Main Board from the Toroid power supply, in the base of the Power Module, to the Main Board. There is a cable on the front of the Main Board from this Toroid power supply which is a FRU-2. There are also test points for the Power Module Toroids (L1, L2, and L3. These Toroids are FRU-1's). Also, check the test points on the Main Board to test power to the Transistor Shelf and the PPBM. Check fuses F1, and F2 located on the back of the Power Module.

title: 2239281 - EM_GDT_STAT_NO_GRAM_CFG
body:
ERROR: EM_GDT_STAT_NO_GRAM_CFG
GRADIENT DRIVER TESTS - %b Tests %c Axis GRAM Configuration Error. The GRAM DIP switch on the MIF is not set, but software detects a GRAM present. To test this axis, change the GRAM DIP switch and run test again.
Extended error: If power is applied to the GRAM, and the DIP switch is in the no GRAM position, and you are trying to troubleshoot by bypassing the GRAM, then, the GRAM has to be taken out of the circuit. The GRAM has to be wired out of the circuit, not just turned off when bypassing the GRAM. If there is no GRAM, but software detects that there is a GRAM, then the DIP switch is not being read properly, this is probably a bad MIF Module. Try toggling the dip switch and re-run this test. If the problem goes away, then the dip switch is probably failing intermittently. Replace the MIF Module. If the problem does not go away, then try swapping the MIF Module and re- running the test. If the problem moves, replace the MIF Module. If the problem stays on the same axis, then there is probably a cable problem. Re-check the cable connections and run numbers.

title: 2239306 - EM_GDT_STAT_VOUTL_RDYVCC
body:
ERROR: EM_GDT_STAT_VOUTL_RDYVCC
GRADIENT DRIVER TESTS - Static Test Failed on %c Axis. VOUT_L had %d failures out of %d. Possible causes: 8645 LOW Main Board, Output Shelf, PPBM, MIF Module, GRAM Module (if present), or Load. Ready Vctrl=1 AVin=0
Extended error: To ensure functionality of the ASM Board, swap the ASM Board for this axis with the ASM Board of another axis and re-test. If the error moves, change the ASM Board. If the problem stays on the same axis, follow the suggested service method in these error messages. If the system has previously reported an Amp Overcurrent or Current Distortion error, and it fails this test, then just about everything in the Power Module and the Load is in the category where it could be suspected as bad. There is probably only one FRU that is bad. A suggested Service Method is to disconnect the Load from the output of the Power Module and run this test again. If the test passes this time, then there is a problem with the Load. The Load test, which is the next test run, will fail generating an error message.

body:

GRADIENT DRIVER TESTS - Static Test Failed on %c Axis. IOUT_H had %d failures out of %d. Possible causes: 8645 HI Main Board, Current Shunt, Output Shelf, MIF, Epoxy-filled Gradient Coil, Output cables, or Gradient Filter Box. Ready Vctrl=1 AVin=0
Extended error: To ensure functionality of the ASM Board, swap the ASM Board for this axis with the ASM Board of another axis and re-test. If the error moves, change the ASM Board. If the problem stays on the same axis, follow the suggested service method in these error messages. This is an indication that there is a problem outside of this Power Module. However, if the tests stop at this point again, then the problem is inside of the affected Power Module or the MIF Module. This is the first error message that will come up after current is applied during the Gradient Driver Tests. Try performing the Load Continuity Test procedure to ensure the load is not open. GRADIENT DRIVER TESTS - Static Test Failed on %c Axis. I_COIL had %d failures out of %d. Possible causes: GRAM Module, Epoxy Filled Gradient Coil, Gradient Filter Box, or Output Cables. Ready Vctrl=1 AVin=0
Extended error: To ensure functionality of the ASM Board, swap the ASM Board for this axis with the ASM Board of another axis and re-test. If the error moves, change the ASM Board. if the problem stays on the same axis, follow troubleshooting advice in the error message from the error log or extended error log when appropriate. To ensure functionality of the GASM, swap the GASM Board for this axis with a GASM Board of another axis and re-test. If the error moves, change the GASM Board. If the problem stays on the same axis, follow troubleshooting advice in the error message from the error log or extended error log when appropriate. The test that produces this error message is trying to measure the resistance or conductance of the load. One of the failures could be an open or a short. A very hot Gradient Coil could be the source of this error as well. To check the continuity of the Gradient Coil and the rest of the Gradient Driver Subsystem, follow procedure for Continuity Test. To swap the GRAM Module, use the GRAM Troubleshooting Harness. Remember to swap the appropriate status and control cables at the bottom of the rear of the GRAM Cabinet.

d) >800,000 Amp transitions/sec (OCDUTY LED DS6) If this condition, suspect the PSD. Remove the JP1 located on miniGRAM control Board to latch the appropriate LED. If this error occurs 4 more times, 2241548 will be reported and you will have to cycle power to the GRAM Power Supply to reset it.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2241515 - EM_GIP_MGRAM_OV_FAULT
body:
ERROR: EM_GIP_MGRAM_OV_FAULT
The GIP reported a %c Axis miniGRAM OverVoltage Fault. Try swapping the miniGRAM Control Board, or the entire miniGRAM axis, or the miniGRAM Power Supply to isolate the problem.
Extended error: This occurs if miniGRAM Power Supply voltage is > 850 VDC. Measure the voltage at J2 on the front of the miniGRAM Control Board; pin 8(Vbus+), pin 20(Vbus-) should be 7.5V + 0.3V. Swap miniGRAM cables to isolate between miniGRAM and miniGRAM Power Supply. If error follows miniGRAM, swap miniGRAM Control Boards to further isolate cause and replace the defective component. If this error occurs 4 more times, 2241547 will be reported and you will have to cycle power to the GRAM Power Supply to reset it.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2241516 - EM_GIP_MGRAM_UV_FAULT
body:

The GIP reported a %c Axis miniGRAM UnderVoltage Fault. Try swapping the miniGRAM Control Board, or the entire miniGRAM axis, or the miniGRAM Power Supply to isolate the problem.
Extended error: This error occurs if the miniGRAM Power Supply voltage is < 300VDC. Measure the voltage at J2 on the front of the miniGRAM Control Board; pins 8(Vbus+), 20(Vbus-) should be 7.5V + 0.3V. Swap miniGRAM cables to isolate between miniGRAM and miniGRAM Power Supply. If error follows miniGRAM, swap miniGRAM Control Boards to further isolate cause and replace the defective component.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2241517 - EM_GIP_GPM_XSISTOR_FAULT
body:
ERROR: EM_GIP_GPM_XSISTOR_FAULT
The GIP reported a Transistor Fault on the %c Axis of the GPM. This fault could be related to noise. Possible causes: Cable between the GIP and GPM, %c Axis GPM Main Board or Output Shelf.
Extended error: If the transistor fault happens immediately when the scanner goes to Ready, this indicates a shorted transistor and the Output Shelf for this axis will have to be replaced. If this error occurs 4 more times, 2241546 will be reported and you will have to cycle power to the GPM Power Supply to reset it. If the fault is intermittent, swap the GPM Main Board for the failing axis with another Main Board to isolate the cause of the fault to the Main Board or the Output Shelf. Replace the component that reproduces the fault.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2241518 - EM_GIP_GPMPS_FAULT
body:
ERROR: EM_GIP_GPMPS_FAULT
The GIP reported a GPM Power Supply Fault. Check the GPM or the GPM Power Supply.
Extended error: This error can be caused by Overtemp, Overcurrent, or Overvoltage conditions on GPM Power Supply. If the error occurs 4 more times, error 2241550 will be generated and power to the GPM Power Supply will need to be cycled to reset it. If error sequence reoccurs then remove output cables from the back of the GPM one at a time to isolate to GPM axis (you must always have at least one output connected or a Power Supply fault will occur.). Note: while running with an output disconnected from an axis, you can ignore error 2241522 or 2242045 for that axis.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2241519 - EM_GIP_MGRAMPS_FAULT
body:
ERROR: EM_GIP_MGRAMPS_FAULT
The GIP reported a miniGRAM Power Supply Fault. Check GRAM Tuning, the miniGRAM, or the miniGRAM Power Supply.
Extended error: This error can be caused by Overtemp, Overcurrent, or Overvoltage conditions on GRAM Power Supply. If this error occurs 4 more times, error 2241549 will be genera ted and then power to the GRAM Power Supply will need to be cycled to reset it. If the error sequence reoccurs then remove output cables from miniGRAM's one at a time to isolate to an axis (you must always have at least one output connected or an Overload error will stop the diagnostics). Note: while running with an output disconnected from an axis, you can ignore error 2241516 or 2242039 for that axis.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2241520 - EM_GIP_MGRAM_IDIST_FAULT
body:
ERROR: EM_GIP_MGRAM_IDIST_FAULT
The GIP reported a %c Axis Current Distortion Fault. Another fault reported in the log could be the cause of this fault. Possible causes: GRAM Tuning, miniGRAM, components of the %c Axis GPM, GIP, or cables.
Extended error: The output current did not follow the commanded current. If this error is reported following another fault that shuts don the axis, focus on troubleshooting the previous error reported. Other causes: If this is a new installation, check output cabling to the gradient coil. Connect scope to DAC_I for appropriate axis on 37 sub-D connector on front GIP panel. Connect scope ground to gnd. on GIP front panel. Signal at ICOIL BNC for appropriate axis on 37 sub-D connector on front of GIP panel should be identical but inverted.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2241521 - EM_GIP_GPM_SHELF_OT_FAULT
body:
ERROR: EM_GIP_GPM_SHELF_OT_FAULT
The GIP reported a Shelf Over Temp Fault on the %c Axis of the GPM. Wait for the temperature to cool before trying to scan. Cooling time may be in excess of 5 minutes. Make sure back door of Gradient Cabinet is closed.
Extended error: The Shelf Overtemp Fault is sensed on the GPM. Check for the following:
a) Verify backdoor of gradient cabinet is closed
b) Excessive output current 9>100A RMS)
c) PPBM Vrail output malfuntion. Vrail could be stuck at high voltage ~190V.
d) If the scanner was using a custom PSD, suspect the PSD
e) If none of the above causes are the problem, then isolate between Main Board and Output Shelf for the failing axis by swapping with another axis.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2241522 - EM_GIP_GPM_SUPPLY_FAULT
body:
ERROR: EM_GIP_GPM_SUPPLY_FAULT
The GIP reported a PPBM Fault on the %c Axis of the GPM. The GPM will recover when the Supply voltage changes to a
safe range. Possible causes: %c Axis GPM PPBM, Main Board, Output Shelf, or the GPM Power Supply.
Extended error: This error is generated by the PPBM and would occur under the following conditions
a) PPBM was Overtemp
b) Input voltage from GPM Power Supply (in Ready) was <80V or >210V
c) Average output current >100A. If these are not the problem, then replace the PPBM. If the error is intermittent, swap PPBM's.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2241523 - EM_GIP_GPM_LONG_OVERLOAD_FAULT
body:
ERROR: EM_GIP_GPM_LONG_OVERLOAD_FAULT
The GIP reported a Long Overload Fault on the %c Axis of the GPM.
Possible causes: %c Axis GPM. Try swapping the GPM Axis connections to isolate the problem.
Extended error: Long overload (overload that is >50 msec in duration) is sensed on the GPM when the output voltage does not follow the commanded voltage. Use a scope to verify the input signal VCNTRL for appropriate axis on front panel of GIP and the output signal on GPM BNC (Vout) are the same. Connect scope ground to gnd on GIP. Long Overloads will shutdown scan and could be indicative of image quality or stability problems.

title: 2241537 - EM_GIP_GPM_FAILED_READY
body:
ERROR: EM_GIP_GPM_FAILED_READY
The %c Axis of the GPM failed to go to Ready when commanded. Check the cable between the GIP & GPM, and the LED status on the %c Axis of the GPM. Guarantee that the switch on the GPM is set to GIP Control. Swap axis GPM Main Bd.
Extended error: If the GPM failed to go to Ready when commanded, the GPM to GIP cable is suspect. Or there could be a fault on the GPM that is not being reported to the GIP. The faults can be seen by viewing the LED's through the Main Board Tray by pulling the GPM out momentarily (Remember, do not scan with the GPM pulled out of the cabinet, because the GPM needs the air flow from the cabinet). Note: it is normal for the Standby LED or the Ready LED on the GPM to be lit when the GPM PS is not enabled.

The GIP reported a PPBM Fault on the %c Axis of the GPM. The GPM will recover when the Supply voltage changes to a
safe range. Possible causes: %c Axis GPM PPBM, Main Board, Output Shelf, or the GPM Power Supply.
Extended error: This fault occurs when the GPM initially goes to Ready when commanded, but then gets an error while in Ready. This fault is generated by the PPBM and will occur with any of the following conditions:
a) Overtemp

c) Average output current >100A. If these are not the problem, then replace the PPBM. If the fault is intermittent, swap PPBM's to verify the failure. If swapping does not confirm a bad PPBM the error could be due to the GPM main board, output shelf, or the GIP.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2242037 - EM_SGDT_MGRAM_OC_FAULT
body:
ERROR: EM_SGDT_MGRAM_OC_FAULT
GRADIENT DRIVER TESTS - %c Axis Fault Occurred. The GIP reported a %c Axis miniGRAM OverCurrent Fault. Try swapping the miniGRAM Control Board, or entire miniGRAM axis, or miniGRAM Gate Driver Bd, or GPM, or GIP to isolate problem. %b
Extended error: The following conditions can cause this ERROR:
a) >140A average current (OCAVG LED DS7)
b) >275A peak current (OCINST LED DS8)
c) >80% Pulse Width Modulation (OCDUTY LED DS6)
d) >800,000 Amp transitions/sec (OCDUTY LED DS6) If this condition, suspect the PSD. Remove the JP1 located on miniGRAM control Board to latch the appropriate LED. If this error occurs 4 more times, 2241548 will be reported and you will have to cycle power to the GRAM Power Supply to reset it.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2242038 - EM_SGDT_MGRAM_OV_FAULT
body:
ERROR: EM_SGDT_MGRAM_OV_FAULT
GRADIENT DRIVER TESTS - %c Axis Fault Occurred. The GIP reported a %c Axis miniGRAM OverVoltage Fault. Try swapping the miniGRAM Control Board, or the entire miniGRAM axis, or the miniGRAM Power Supply to isolate the problem. %b
Extended error: This occurs if miniGRAM Power Supply voltage is > 850 VDC. Measure the voltage at J2 on the front of the miniGRAM Control Board; pins 8(Vbus+), 20(Vbus-) should be 7.5V + 0.3V. Swap miniGRAM cables to isolate between miniGRAM and miniGRAM Power Supply. If error follows miniGRAM, swap miniGRAM Control Boards to further isolate cause and replace the defective component. If this error occurs 4 more times, 2241547 will be reported and you will have to cycle power to the GRAM Power Supply to reset it.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2242039 - EM_SGDT_MGRAM_UV_FAULT
body:
ERROR: EM_SGDT_MGRAM_UV_FAULT
GRADIENT DRIVER TESTS - %c Axis Fault Occurred. The GIP reported a %c Axis miniGRAM UnderVoltage Fault. Try swapping the miniGRAM Control Board, or the entire miniGRAM axis, or the miniGRAM Power Supply to isolate the problem. %b
Extended error: This error occurs if the miniGRAM Power Supply voltage is < 300VDC. Measure the voltage at J2 on the front of the miniGRAM Control Board; pins 8(Vbus+), 20(Vbus-) should be 7.5V + 0.3V. Swap miniGRAM cables to isolate between miniGRAM and miniGRAM Power Supply. If error follows miniGRAM, swap miniGRAM Control Boards to further isolate cause and replace the defective component.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2242040 - EM_SGDT_GPM_XSISTOR_FAULT
body:
ERROR: EM_SGDT_GPM_XSISTOR_FAULT
GRADIENT DRIVER TESTS - %c Axis Fault Occurred. The GIP reported a Transistor Fault on the %c Axis of the GPM. This fault could be related to noise. Possible causes: Cable between the GIP and GPM, Axis GPM Main Board or Output Shelf. %b
Extended error: If the transistor fault happens immediately when the scanner goes to Ready, this indicates a shorted transistor and the Output Shelf for this axis will have to be replaced. If this error occurs 4 more times, 2241546 will be reported and you will have to cycle power to the GPM Power Supply to reset it. If the fault is intermittent, swap the GPM Main Board for the failing axis with another Main Board to isolate the cause of the fault to the Main Board or the Output Shelf. Replace the component that reproduces the fault.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2242041 - EM_SGDT_GPMPS_FAULT
body:
ERROR: EM_SGDT_GPMPS_FAULT
GRADIENT DRIVER TESTS - Fault Occurred. The GIP reported a GPM Power Supply Fault. Check the GPM or the GPM Power Supply. %b
Extended error: This error can be caused by Overtemp, Overcurrent, or Overvoltage conditions on GPM Power Supply. If the error occurs 4 more times, error 2241550 will be generated and power to the GPM Power Supply will need to be cycled to reset it. If error sequence reoccurs then remove output cables from the back of the GPM one at a time to isolate to GPM axis (you must always have at least one output connected or a Power Supply fault will occur.). Note: while running with an output disconnected from an axis, you can ignore error 2241522 or 2242045 for that axis.

If this error occurs 4 more times, error 2241549 will be genera ted and then power to the GRAM Power Supply will need to be cycled to reset it. If the error sequence reoccurs then remove output cables from miniGRAM's one at a time to isolate to an axis (you must always have at least one output connected or an Overload error will stop the diagnostics). title: 2242127 - EM_SGDT_STAT_VRAIL_RDYGRAM
body:
ERROR: EM_SGDT_STAT_VRAIL_RDYGRAM
GRADIENT DRIVER TESTS - Static Test Failed on %c Axis. VRAIL had %d failures out of %d. Possible causes: GIP Bd, the load, miniGRAM, this axis of the GPM, or GPM Power Supply. Static Ready GRAM Mode
Extended error: Swap miniGRAM and GPM data cables at GIP reports problem on same axis, replace the GIP. If not then swap load cables at the back of miniGRAM's. If problem followed axes next isolate between miniGRAM and GPM (in main bd, PPBM and output shelf order). Then turn off power to gradient cabinet and disconnect GRAM output cables. Then check load resistance across terminals of the BRM (0.2 ohms); from terminal of load to ground (>1K ohms); and terminal of each axis to other axes (>1K ohms). Lastly GPM Power Supply. Note: use the disconnection and drive one axis at a time information in previous message

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2244570 - EM_GP_SGA_FAILED_READY
body:
ERROR: EM_GP_SGA_FAILED_READY
The %c Axis gradient amplifier failed to go to Ready when commanded. Please perform a TPS reset and try again. If the problem persists, please call service engineer.
Extended error: If the G_ENABLE test point on J2(front of SGA/HFA)is high(5V), the problem is likely in the gradient amplifier or power supply. Swap Gradient Amplifier Control Board with that of another axis to isolate Gradient Amplifier vs. Gradient Amplifier Control Board. If the G_ENABLE test point is low, check the cable between GP and the Gradient Amplifier, or replace the GP.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)

If no LEDs are lit on the front of the Gradient Amplifier, swap 208V line cables with another axis, or swap Gradient Control Boards with another axis. If fault persists and does not follow cable or Control Board, replace the Gradient Amplifier.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2244606 - EM_GP_SGAPS_OT_SPECIAL_RECV
body:
ERROR: EM_GP_SGAPS_OT_SPECIAL_RECV
The GP reported multiple SGA Power Supply Overtemperature Faults.
Extended error: Check that cabinet fan is functioning properly, rear door is closed and sealed and that no filler panels have been removed from the front of the cabinet. Proper cooling requires a vaccum to pull air through the Gradient Amplifiers, Power Supply, and GP. If fault persists on specific PSDs, write a PQR. If fault persists on many or all PSDs, replace SGA Power Supply. TPS Reset is required to recover from this fault.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2244607 - EM_GP_SGAPS_UV_SPECIAL_RECV
body:
ERROR: EM_GP_SGAPS_UV_SPECIAL_RECV
The GP reported mutiple SGA Power Supply UnderVoltage Faults.
Extended error: Look at the SGAPS UV LEDs on the front of the module to determine which axis caused the fault. If the BUS_UV LED is lit, check the 420V input to the SGA Power Supply from the PDU. If the UV_X,Y,Z LED is lit, swap military connectors to the Gradient Amplifiers to isolate Gradient Amplifier vs. SGA Power Supply. TPS Reset is required to recover from this fault.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2244845 - EM_GP_SGA_IDIST_SPECIAL_RECV
body:
ERROR: EM_GP_SGA_IDIST_SPECIAL_RECV
The GP reported mutliple Gradient Amplifier %c Axis Current Distortion Faults.
Extended error: This is a generic fault message indicating that the Gradient Amplifiers are not accurately following the current command from the IPG/SRF. If other faults occurred concurrently, they will provide useful information to assist with troubleshooting. Else, swap the control cable between the GP and the failing Gradient Amplifier with the Gradient Amplifier on another axis (swap one end of the cable only). If the fault moves, replace the Gradient Amplifier or Gradient Amplifier Control Board (board can be swapped with another axis to isolate), or check the gradient coil. If the fault does not move, replace the GP.

title: 2244857 - EM_GP_SGAPS_POWER_OFF_FAULT
body:
ERROR: EM_GP_SGAPS_POWER_OFF_FAULT
The GP is reporting SGA Power Supply Power Off Fault.
Extended error: Please check MRconfig.cfg file to determine the amplifier type, 8915-ACGD, 8916-HFD. ACGD MESSAGE: Check the ACGD Power (or ACGD 420V Power) breaker on the PDU. If breaker is tripped, replace the SGA Power Supply. Notice: Do not attempt to reset the breaker! Press the EMO Reset Button on the PDU. Check J2 on the rear of the PDU for continuity between pins 7 and 8. Check phase rotation by confirming that the gradient fan is rotating correctly, or that the Phase OK" light is lit for newer PDUs. Else, replace the SGA Power Supply. HFD MESSAGE: Check the ACGD 420V Power breaker on the PDU. If breaker is tripped, replace the SGA Power Supply. Notice: Do not attempt to reset the breaker! Press the EMO Reset Button on the PDU. Check J2 on the rear of the PDU for continuity between pins 7 and 8. Check the "Phase OK" light on the front of the PDU. Else, replace the SGA Power Supply."

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2244859 - EM_GP_SGAPS_OT_FAULT
body:
ERROR: EM_GP_SGAPS_OT_FAULT
The GP is reporting a SGA Power Supply OverTemperature Fault. System will wait five minutes before attempting recovery.
Extended error: Check that cabinet fan is functioning properly, rear door is closed and sealed and that no filler panels have been removed from the front of the cabinet. Proper cooling requires a vaccum to pull air through the Gradient Amplifiers, Power Supply, and GP. Low Equipment Room air temperature can also cause this fault. Verify Equipment Room temperature is not below recommended limit. If fault persists on specific PSDs, write a PQR. If fault persists on many or all PSDs, replace SGA Power Supply.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2244860 - EM_GP_SGAPS_OC_FAULT
body:

Extended error: If this fault is intermittent, temporarily remove jumper J1 on the SGA Power Supply Control Board to prevent automatic recovery. When the fault recurs, look at SGAPS OC LEDs on the front to determine which axis caused the fault. If the primary OC LED is lit replace SGA Power Supply. If a secondary OC LED is lit, swap military connectors to the Gradient Amplifiers to isolate Gradient Amplifier vs. SGA Power Supply. For more information, open the Common Service Desktop and go to Service Docs - Peripherals - Gradient Electronics 2244590 Extended Help.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: Gradient Power Supply, Gradient Amp

title: 2245043 - EM_ACGDT_SGAPS_POWER_OFF_FAULT
body:
ERROR: EM_ACGDT_SGAPS_POWER_OFF_FAULT
GRADIENT DRIVER TESTS - The GP is reporting SGA-PS Power Supply Power Off Fault. %b
Extended error: Please check MRconfig.cfg file to determine the amplifier type, 8915-ACGD, 8916-HFD. ACGD MESSAGE: Check the ACGD Power (or ACGD 420V Power) breaker on the PDU. If breaker is tripped, replace the SGA Power Supply. Notice: Do not attempt to reset the breaker! Press the EMO Reset Button on the PDU. Check J2 on the rear of the PDU for continuity between pins 7 and 8. Check phase rotation by confirming that the gradient fan is rotating correctly, or that the Phase OK" light is lit for newer PDUs. Else, replace the SGA Power Supply. HFD MESSAGE: Check the ACGD 420V Power breaker on the PDU. If breaker is tripped, replace the SGA Power Supply. Notice: Do not attempt to reset the breaker! Press the EMO Reset Button on the PDU. Check J2 on the rear of the PDU for continuity between pins 7 and 8. Check the "Phase OK" light on the front of the PDU. Else, replace the SGA Power Supply."

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2245053 - EM_ACGDT_SGA_IDIST_RDY_FAULT
body:
ERROR: EM_ACGDT_SGA_IDIST_RDY_FAULT
GRADIENT DRIVER TESTS - The GP is reporting a Gradient Amplifier %c Axis Current Distortion Fault. %b
Extended error: This is a generic fault message indicating that the Gradient Amplifiers are not accurately following the current command from the IPG/SRF. If other faults occurred concurrently, they will provide useful information to assist with troubleshooting. Else, swap the control cable between the GP and the failing Gradient Amplifier with the Gradient Amplifier on another axis (swap one end of the cable only). If the fault moves, replace the Gradient Amplifier or Gradient Amplifier Control Board (board can be swapped with another axis to isolate), or check the gradient coil. If the fault does not move, check the PSD or replace the GP.

Extended error: Check tuning in gradient_tune.dat file. Swap amplifier axis by swapping cables between the GP and HFA (between the failing axis and a passing axis), and also swapping gradient output leads on the same two Gradient Amplifiers. If the problem moves, replace the HFA or HFA Control Board (Boards can be swapped with another axis to isolate HFA vs. Control Board). Else, check the gradient coil resistance to ground or replace the GP. While this error could indicate a hardware failure, please also check that HFA Control Boards are installed in the front of each gradient amplifier. Using SGA Control Boards instead of HFA Control Boards will cause this error.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2246201 - EM_DMAAPI_CLOSE_INVALID_BOARD_CHANNEL_SEMAPHORE_ID
body:
ERROR: EM_DMAAPI_CLOSE_INVALID_BOARD_CHANNEL_SEMAPHORE_ID
DMA API - Close operation failed because the DMA interface handle's semaphore is no longer valid.
Extended error: When a DMA interface is opened a semaphore, which uniquely identifies the board and channel used for the DMA transfer, is created. The semaphore ID is stored in the DMA interface handle. When the DMA interface is closed using plxDmaClose(), the semaphore is 'given' using semGive(), and deleted using semDelete(). This error occurred because the semGive(<sempahore ID from DMA interface handle>) function failed. Either (1) the sempahore environment of the O/S is corrupted, or (2) the DMA interface handle is corrupted.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: Firmware

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2246202 - EM_DMAAPI_CLOSE_INVALID_BLOCKING_SEMAPHORE_ID
body:
ERROR: EM_DMAAPI_CLOSE_INVALID_BLOCKING_SEMAPHORE_ID
DMA API - Close operation failed because the blocking semaphore is no longer valid.
Extended error: When a DMA interface is opened, the software defaults the transfer to a blocking transfer - meaning the task initiating the DMA transfer will suspend itself until the DMA transfer is complete. Therefore, a blocking semaphore is created. (Note: If the transfer is non-blocking, the sempahore is deleted and this error cannot occur.) The semaphore ID is stored in the DMA interface handle. For blocking transfers, when the DMA interface is closed using plxDmaClose(), the semaphore is 'given' using semGive(), and deleted using semDelete(). This error occurred because the semGive(<blocking sempahore ID from DMA interface handle>) function failed. Either (1) the sempahore environment of the O/S is corrupted, or (2) the DMA interface handle is corrupted.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: Firmware

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2246203 - EM_DMAAPI_CLOSE_C6X_HPI_CLOSE_FAILED
body:
ERROR: EM_DMAAPI_CLOSE_C6X_HPI_CLOSE_FAILED
DMA API - Close operation failed because the HPI interface, used for DMA transfers to 16 bit memory, could not be successfully closed.
Extended error: DMA transfers to 16 bit memory require transfers to 32 bit Fast Update and 32 bit Burst memory. On-board hardware decode logic detects write transactions to Fast Update and Burst memory, and then initiate write transactions to 16 bit memory through the HPI interface. To ensure exclusive access to HPI hardware, software interfaces are used. During plcDmaSetup(), an HPI interface is opened (reserved for exclusive use) when the destination DMA location is Fast Update or Burst memory. The HPI interface is stored in the DMA interface handle. When the DMA interface is closed using plxDmaClose(), the HPI handle is closed. This error occurred because HPI close operation failed. Either (1) the HPI API environment is corrupted, or (2) the DMA interface handle is corrupted.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: Firmware

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2246204 - EM_DMAAPI_OPEN_BOARD_LACKS_DMA_CNTLR
body:
ERROR: EM_DMAAPI_OPEN_BOARD_LACKS_DMA_CNTLR
DMA API - Open operation failed because the board specified for the DMA transfer, as reported by the board support package (BSP), does not have a resident DMA controller.
Extended error: BOARD_TYPE, which is the second parameter of plxDmaOpen(), is the enumerated value that defines which board is responsible for performing the DMA transfer. This parameter is a valid BOARD_TYPE value. However, the DMA API initializes a board definitions table, gstrBoardDefs[] (indexed by BOARD_TYPE), that defines various board parameters related to performing DMA transfers. The table element bDmaResident is based on an element bDmaIsResident in the static table gstrBoardTypeInfo[] (defined in dmaSys.c). This element indicates the board specified in the open operation does not support DMA transfers - meaning a DMA controller is not resident.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: Firmware

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2246205 - EM_DMAAPI_SETUPHPI_HPI_HANDLE_ALREADY_DEFINED
body:
ERROR: EM_DMAAPI_SETUPHPI_HPI_HANDLE_ALREADY_DEFINED
DMA API - Setup HPI operation failed because the HPI interface was already opened by a previous DMA setup or setup HPI function operation.
Extended error: HPI hardware, which provides access to 16 bit memory resident on custom boards, is controlled by a software interface that ensures exclusive access. The HPI interface is used by the DMA API and other software, but can also be shared provided the 'other' software supervises the shared HPI interface. If the DMA API controls (is responsible for opening/closing the HPI interface), the HPI interface, call sequence is plxDmaOpen(), then plxDmaSetup(). If the 'supervisory' software will control the HPI interface, the call sequence is:
plxDmaOpen(), plxDmaSetupHpi(), then plxDmaSetup(). If the HPI interface handle is not defined when plxDmaSetup() is called for the first time, the DMA API takes control of the HPI interface. Otherwise, the DMA API assumes the calling software is supervising the HPI which had to be communicated using the plxDmaSetupHpi() function. This error is a result of plxDmaSetupHpi() being called when the HPI interface handle stored in the DMA interface handle already exists. Either (1) the DMA interface handle is corrupted, (2) plxDmaSetupHpi() was called mulitple times, or
(3) plxDmaSetupHpi() was called after plxDmaSetup().
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: Firmware

title: 2246259 - EM_DMA_DIAGS_FAILED_DATA_MISMATCH
body:
ERROR: EM_DMA_DIAGS_FAILED_DATA_MISMATCH
DMA Diagnostics failed because the data that was transferred did not compare to the original (source) data.
Extended error: A data mismatch indicates that the software set up and started the DMA transfer(s), but the data DMA'ed to a destination memory region did not compare to the original source data. Block DMA and Scatter/ Gather DMAs transfer data from processor memory to custom memory, then back to processor memory. The source and DMA'ed data in processor memory is compared. DMA transfers to Burst and Fast Update memory, which use the HPI interface, DMA data to the respective memory reegion, which the HPI interface transfers to 16 bit memory. The DMA diag then performs discrete reads from the 16 bit memory, copying the data back to processor memory. Again, the source and destination data resident in processor memory is compared. The Demand Mode diag, performs discrete writes to to custom memory. Certain data patterns trigger the custom board's hardware to initiate a DMA transfer back to processor memory. Data in the processor's memory is again compared.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: Firmware

Extended error: Once the DMA transfer is initiated, a semTake() function call attempts to take a blocking semaphore that is not available until the DMA ISR handler frees the blocking semaphore. The second parameter in the semTake() function specifies the duration to wait for the blocking semaphore to become available. The following conditions may exist:
(1) A lengthy DMA transfer did not complete in the timeframe allotted. The timeout parameter should be increased. (2) The ISR handler was not called because of a hardware or O/S error. After the timeout occurred, software attempted to clean up the hardware by aborting the DMA transfer. The cleanup was successful.

title: 2246276 - EM_DMAAPI_SEMTAKE_TIMEOUT_ABORT_FAILED
body:
ERROR: EM_DMAAPI_SEMTAKE_TIMEOUT_ABORT_FAILED
DMA API - The start operation failed. The DMA transfer did not complete prior to the timeout specified in the semTake() function call. Hardware cleanup failed.
Extended error: Once the DMA transfer is initiated, a semTake() function call attempts to take a blocking semaphore that is not available until the DMA ISR handler frees the blocking semaphore. The second parameter in the semTake() function specifies the duration to wait for the blocking semaphore to become available. The following conditions may exist:
(1) A lengthy DMA transfer did not complete in the timeframe allotted. The timeout parameter should be increased. (2) The ISR handler was not called because of a hardware or O/S error.\n After the timeout occurred, software attempted to clean up the hardware by aborting the DMA transfer. The cleanup failed. The DMA controller is in an uncertain state.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: Firmware

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2247153 - EM_IRF_DRVR_NO_RRF_FOUND
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF_DRVR_NO_RRF_FOUND
RF SUBSYSTEM NOT RESPONDING The RRF chassis is not communicating to the MGD chassis. Try TPS Reset. If this problem repeats, call service. Scanning will not be possible. Verify that the RRF chassis is powered on.
Extended error: Check for the GB0 LED on the IRF board in the MGD chassis. The GB0 LED is for RRF channels 1-8. The GB1 LED is for channels 9-16. A fiber cable must connect the DIF board in RRF chassis front slot 10 to the IRFIO board in the rear of the MGD chassis. The top 6 DIF LEDs should be on.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: IRF Board, IRF I/O Board, RRF-DIF Board, Exciter Board, GigaLink Fiber Cable

title: 2247155 - EM_IRF_DRVR_IS8_SHOULD_BE_16CH_ERROR
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF_DRVR_IS8_SHOULD_BE_16CH_ERROR
ONLY 8 OF 16 RF RECEIVER CHANNELS PRESENT This system is configured for 16 RF Receiver channels but channels 9-16 in the RRF chassis are not responding. 16 channel scans will not be possible. 1 to 8 channel scans might work.
Extended error: Check the GB0 and GB1 LEDs on the IRF board in the MGD chassis. The GB0 LED is for RRF channels 1-8. The GB1 LED is for channels 9-16. A fiber cable must connect the 2nd DIF board in RRF chassis front slot 1 to the GB1 connector on the front of the IRF board in the MGD chassis. The top 6 LEDs on the 2nd DIF board should be on.
Make sure that the option key configuration matches the hardware configuration. If this system does not have the hardware installed that is needed for 16 channel scans, the 16 channel option key should not be installed.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: IRF Board, RRF-DIF Board, GigaLink Fiber Cable

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2247156 - EM_IRF_DRVR_IRF2_NOT_DETECTED_ERR
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF_DRVR_IRF2_NOT_DETECTED_ERR
The APS did not detect the IRF2 board in the MGD chassis. The system will not function without this board. This could also indicate a bad AGP, APS or Bridge Board, please check for other error messages.
Extended error: This error indicates that the IRF board failed to be sensed after a hardware reset. This error can be caused by a missing board, a bad backplane, or a bad APS or AGP. This system is not compatible with the original IRF board. If the board is present, try to reseat the board and rerun the test. If other boards are pass their BLD diagnostics, the AGP and APS are probably OK.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: IRF Board, MGD Backplane, APS Board, AGP Board

title: 2247159 - EM_IRF_DRVR_SINE_LUT_LOAD_FAIL_ERR
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF_DRVR_SINE_LUT_LOAD_FAIL_ERR
The Sine Wave Table on the DIF board in RRF chassis (front, slot 10) did not load correctly. This will prevent proper Exciter output. Try TPS_reset. Run RRF diagnostics. Reported from %s (%X) (%X) (%d)
Extended error: At reset the DIF board loads a Sine wave table from an internal EPROM. The DIF did not load the EPROM into Ram correctly. The exciter will not be able to output the correct waveforms if the Sine LUT does not contain the correct data.

Extended error: The broadband Exciter 1.0 is not supported by this system. The Exciter1.0 should have been replaced when this system was upgraded. A broadband Exciter1A was found in the master exciter slot of the RRF chassis. This might degrade image quality. Normally, only the Exciter2 is used as a master and Exciter1A is optionally used as a slave.
Extended error: The broadband Exciter 1A (also known as an Exciter 1.1) should only be used as the slave exciter in a system equipped for MNS. Although the Exciter1A will function as a master, its output signal has more noise than the narrowband Exciter2.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: Exciter Board

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2247166 - EM_IRF_DRVR_IS16_SHOULD_BE_32CH_ERROR
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF_DRVR_IS16_SHOULD_BE_32CH_ERROR
ONLY 16 OF 32 RF RECEIVER CHANNELS PRESENT This system is configured for 32 RF Receiver channels but some or all of the channels in the 2nd RRF chassis are not responding. 32 channel scans will not be possible. 8 or 16 channel scans should work.
Extended error: Check the GB0 - GB3 LEDs on the IRF board in the MGD chassis. For a 32 channel system, they all should be on. The GB0 LED is for RRF channels 1-8 which is the fiber on the IRFIO board that MUST be connected to the master DIF board in the 1st RRF chassis. The GB1-3 LEDs are for the fiber connectors on the front edge of the IRF2 board. Those three fibers can be connected in any order but a 32ch system expects to see all three fibers connected and active. This system does not see a connection to one or both DIFs in the 2nd RRF chassis.
Make sure that the option key configuration matches the hardware configuration. If this system does not have the hardware installed that is needed for 32 channel scans, the 32 channel option key should not be installed.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: IRF Board, RRF-DIF Board, GigaLink Fiber Cable

Extended error: Check the GB0 - GB3 LEDs on the IRF board in the MGD chassis. For a 32 channel system, they all should be on. The GB0 LED is for RRF channels 1-8 which is the fiber on the IRFIO board that MUST be connected to the master DIF board in the 1st RRF chassis. The GB1-3 LEDs are for the fiber connectors on the front edge of the IRF2 board. Those three fibers can be connected in any order but a 32ch system expects to see all three fibers connected and active. This system does not see a connection to the 2nd DIF in the 1st RRF chassis.
Make sure that the option key configuration matches the hardware configuration. If this system does not have the hardware installed that is needed for 32 channel scans, the 32 channel option key should not be installed.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: IRF Board, RRF-DIF Board, GigaLink Fiber Cable

title: 2247170 - EM_IRF_WRONG_1ST_MASTER_EXCITER_FOR_32CH
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF_WRONG_1ST_MASTER_EXCITER_FOR_32CH
This system does not have a master exciter in the 1st RRF chassis that is compatible with 32 channel scans. The system requires an exciter that can drive a clock signal to the 2nd master exciter.
Extended error: A 32 channel system requires a special master exciter in both RRF chassis. These exciters have an inter-connect cable that allows both exciters to run from the same clock source. The system detected an exciter that does not have this capability. Without this type of exciter, 32-channel scans may be corrupted because the two RRF chassis are not clock synchronized. If this system is not intended to run 32 channel scans, remove the 32 channel option key.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: Exciter Board

body:

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2247384 - EM_RRF_DEAD_CHANNEL_FAILED
body:
ERROR: EM_RRF_DEAD_CHANNEL_FAILED
Test: '%s%s' diagnostic error. The signal's energy level is severely below the what is expected. 'Dead'
channels are: %s
Extended error: Sys Cab and UTNS Bypass Diag: Dead channels while running these diags indicate a problem with a board in the receive chain (MUX, UTNS, Rx), or cables between the boards. Sixteen bad channels (or eight bad channels in an eight channel system would indicate a problem with the signal source, or problems other than the three receive chain boards. Eight bad channels in a 16 channel system would indicate a bad board. Swapping good boards with suspected boards is an effective way to isolate a problem. Problems with banks of channels (1-4, 5-8, etc) may indicate a problem with a receive When individual bad channels (1,8,9,16) may lead to an improperly seated cable.\n 16 Channel Switch diag: If problems exist when running this diagnostic, the Sys Cab Loopback diag should also be performed. If the Sys Cab loopback test fails too, then there is a likely problem inside the system cabinet. If the Sys Cab Loopback diag passes, there is probably a problem between the Mux and the 16 Channel Switch(inclusive). For the 16 Channel Switch results, a failure of all 16 channels would indicate a problem with the switch itself. The ports or hte oscillators could be bad. To test the oscillators, try running the Multi-Coil Receive II Diagnostic. For 8 channel failures, check the switch, corresponding ports, or specific cables. Look for trends in the failures for the various port tests.\n Multi-Coil Receive II Diagnostic: To isolate problems between the LPCA connectors and the 16 Channel Switch, the Sys Cab and 16 Channel Switch Diags should be executed first. In conjunction with those results, conclusions may be drawn as to whether the problem resides in the signals' paths.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: Receiver Board, UTNS Board, MUX Board

title: 2248239 - EM_RRFCAL_GETOFFSETS_VAL_ERROR
body:
ERROR: EM_RRFCAL_GETOFFSETS_VAL_ERROR
ADC offsets calibration validation failed. The acquired ADC offsets are out of tolerance for the following receivers.
Rx=%s%s%s%s%s%s%s%s%s A TPS reset may be necessary.
Extended error: Probable causes for this failure:
1) The software state of the system. The software failed to set a Remote RF value properly, which led to improper data acquisition. A TPS reset can solve software related issues. If the error recurs after a reset, then a hardware problem is more likely.
2) The hardware is causing problems. Repeatable problems may be due to a board failure. There are basically three regions to examine. First, the Exciter may be bad, which would indicate consistently bad results across all channels. Second, the receive data chain within the RRF chassis could be bad. Run MGD Board Level and MGD Data Path diagnostics and then run RRF Board Level and Data Path Diagnostics. If the problem appears to be due to low receive signal on one or more channels then run the RRF Receive Chain FRU Isolation Diagnostic to identify the failing MUX, UTNS3, Receiver, or RRF-DIF Board.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: RRF-DIF Board, Exciter Board, Receiver Board, DRF Board, Firmware

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2248258 - EM_DC_RRF_SER_NUM_UNAVAIL
body:
ERROR: EM_DC_RRF_SER_NUM_UNAVAIL
RRF Serial Number registers not loaded. Presence and validation of Remote RF boards could not be confirmed. Valid status memory reads - %d
Extended error: For each of the Remote RF boards, serial number status memory registers are not available until 7-9 microseconds following reset. The RRF-DIF Status register contains a status bit, Serial Number Loaded from ROM, which indicates the validity of the serial number registers. This bit was polled several times. For each iteration, the status bit is checked to confirm serial number registers were successfully loaded. If valid, polling stops. Otherwise, a WriteWait() call is made in order to allow status memory to be updated for the next polling attempt. If the number of valid status memory reads is 0, status memory is not getting updated.

Value seen: %d, Expected 15000 or greater.
Extended error: In this calibration, the Exciter board is looped back to the Receiver board through the MUX. The Exciter then generates a signal and the Receiver samples it. With max gains and min attenuation, the recovered signal was still too small to use. Check RRF chassis cables. Run the RRF Receive Chain FRU Diagnostic if necessary.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: Exciter Board, Receiver Board, RRF-DIF Board, MUX Board

Extended error: The server listed is not communicating to the SCP. This is either because the server is hung or the communication path is down from it to the SCP. Please check other error messages in the log to see if any of the other servers have reported an error.
The server listed in the error message corresponds to the following physical location:
SC -> SCP board PS -> AGP board AQ -> APS board DP -> AP board(s) DS -> Host computer (dsserver process)
A TPS reset will most likely be required to recover from this problem and if that doesn't work, a system shutdown.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2248589 - EM_HC_KEYBOARD_RX_ERR
body:
ERROR: EM_HC_KEYBOARD_RX_ERR
SCIM Communication Error. The keyboard serial port reported an error upon reception of a character. Serial status: 0x%02X Character: 0x%02X
Extended error: The SCP serial port that communicates to the SCIM reported a serial link error. This could be either a framing error or a receive overrun.
A framing error (Serial status: 0x10) indicates a timing problem on the serial link, which could be caused by an intermittent cable connection, faulty cable, or a faulty SCIM or SCP. This is most likely a cable problem.
An overrun error (Serial status: 0x02) indicates that the SCP could not keep up with the receive data coming from the SCIM. This is most likely a problem with the SCP.
This message might also occur if the power to the SCIM has been shut down while performing system maintenance or if the SCIM power is intermittent.
Check that the SCIM has power, which is supplied via the cable from the GOCAA/WIM.
Check that the communication link is connected between the STIF(or PSE) and the SCIM and that there are no loose connections.
Please run the keyboard (SCIM) diagnostics to locate the problem.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: SCIM, STIF Board, PSE Board, SCP Board

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2248652 - EM_HC_BORE_TEMP_TRIP_2
body:
ERROR: EM_HC_BORE_TEMP_TRIP_2
Scan inhibited. Patient comfort sensor trip.\b\ To return to scanning, verify:
1. Patient fan is ON.
2. Scan room temperature is normal.
3. Air flow through the bore is unobstructed.
4. Gradient Cooling fan is normal.
5. BRM heat exchanger is normal.
Extended error: The bore temp that was measured by the SRI has reached the second trip level. Subsequent scans will not be allowed.
If the bore temperature is not high, this could indicate a problem with the bore temperature sensor cable or the SRI. Please make sure that the bore temperature sensor cable is connected to the SRI and that it is positioned correctly in the bore.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: Bore Temp Sensor, SRI

RF Amplifier Error. The RF amplifier changed state (powered off, went to standby or operate) without being commanded. Previous state: 0x%02X New state: 0x%02X Please power cycle the RF Subsystem and perform a TPS Reset.
Extended error: The RF Amp reported a state change to the SCP when no state change was commanded. This could indicate a problem with CAN Communication, SCP board, or RF Amp. Verify that these components are configured correctly and perform a TPS Reset.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: CAN Communication, SCP Board, RF Amp

Extended error: This test will fail in this way if a loopback connector is not installed on the SCP to SCIM communication path after the STIF(or PSE) board.
If a loopback connector is installed, please try running the SCP internal loopback test. If that test fails, the SCP has failed.
If the SCP loopback test is successful, then the problem could be an issue with the loopback connector, any cable between the loopback connector and the STIF(or PSE) board, the STIF(or PSE) board, the MGD backplane, or the SCP board (in that order).

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2251760 - EM_SGDT_DYN_VCNTRL_FLATLINE
body:
ERROR: EM_SGDT_DYN_VCNTRL_FLATLINE
GRADIENT DRIVER TESTS - Dynamic Test failed on %c Axis. VCNTRL data does not follow the input waveform. Possible causes: Fiber Optic cable between GIP and STIF, or the GIP Board.
Extended error: Check GRAM Tuning first, if it fails then suspect gradient hardware and troubleshoot after putting defaults in for short time constant eddy currents. Swap miniGRAM and GPM data cables at GIP reports problem on same axis, replace the GIP. If not then swap load cables at the back of miniGRAM's. If problem followed axes next isolate between miniGRAM and GPM (in main bd, PPBM and output shelf order). Then turn off power to gradient cabinet and disconnect GRAM output cables. Then check load resistance across terminals of the BRM (0.2 ohms); from terminal of load to ground (>1K ohms); and terminal of each axis to other axes (>1K ohms). Lastly GPM Power Supply. Note: use the disconnection and drive one axis at a time information in previous message
