doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2252112 - EM_MOT_DIAG_INVALID_PWRON_STATE_ERR
body:
ERROR: EM_MOT_DIAG_INVALID_PWRON_STATE_ERR
Board %s is in invalid power up state %d. Verify ENV parameters and retry power up.
Extended error: The board may be in one of the following states:
0 - No response, 1 - OS Loaded, 2 - PPC Bug, 3 - PPC Diag, 4 - OS not loaded
If the error message states that the board is in state 4, then the OS load was stopped. This may happen if characters are detected on the serial cable. In order to eliminate this problem, disconnect the serial cable from AGP/COM1 Connector or SCP/Console Connector and reboot the board. If the error message states that the board is in state 2 or 3, then run the Motorola Board Level Diagnostics to verify the board is OK. If the BLD passes but this message appears during TPS reset then it is highly probable that the boards are not being reset by STIF(or PSE) connection. You can verify if the boards are not being reset by STIF(or PSE) connection during TPS reset either by looking at the LEDs on front of the boards or by opening MGD Terminal window.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2252301 - EM_DCB_MCD_OPEN_CKT
body:
ERROR: EM_DCB_MCD_OPEN_CKT
Multicoil Bias Fault - Open Circuit. Try re-seating all coil connectors.\b\ MCD%d Channel %d of 16, counting from 1
Value: %d mA, Limit: %d mA Mask of failed channels: 0x%x MCD1 1-8 : A or C MCD1 9-16 : B MCD2 1-8 : B or Legacy MC MCD2 9-16 : C
Extended error: This fault was detected by the Driver Module. An open circuit fault occurs when the actual value is less than the pre-defined limit. Check system cables, connectors, coils and configurations. Re-seat all coil connectors. The mask of all failed channels indicates additional channels with the same fault - convert the hex number to a bitmap to decipher the mask, with channel 1 indicated by the least significant bit and channel 16 indicated by the most significant bit. For example, a mask of 0x3c converts to 0011 1100, meaning channels 3, 4, 5, and 6 all experienced the same failure. The key at the bottom of the error message shows the MC driver bias channels provided by the Driver Module used with each multicoil connector. Note that some systems may not have all the connectors listed. Tools such as Gather Load Data located on the CSD Diagnostics page under Peripherals, Driver Module Diagnostics can help with isolating this failure to a coil, cable, LPCA module, or Driver Module.
In 20.0 and later systems, MC bias is supplied and sensed by the RF Hub, so this message should not be logged. TPS reset may help recover.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: Driver Module

body:
ERROR: EM_DCB_THERMAL_TRIP
Body Hybrid Splitter Thermal Trip or Short Circuit Detected.
Value: %d mA Limit: %d mA
Extended error: Excessive reflected power from the body coil has overheated the Body Hybrid or a short circuit condition (failed PIN diode) has occurred in the Body Hybrid Splitter. If this failure is intermittent, check body coil and I/Q cabling. If this failure is hard, check Body Hybrid Splitter and TR bias cabling for short circuits. Use TR DD MC diagnostic to troubleshoot.
In 20.0 and later systems, try running the TR DD System Path diagnostic to troubleshoot.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: Driver Module, Body Hybrid Splitter, Body RF Coil

Num of Pulses Sent: %d.
Num of Pulses Received: %d.
Extended error: The SWIFT Cable is the cable connecting the IRF I/O DAB out port to the Driver Module High Speed Data Port. This test verifies that pulses sent to the Driver Module from the IRF I/O board are sent and received properly. Try a different cable(the cable is not a straight through cable). If not verify the pulses are coming out of the IRF I/O by probing pins 3 and 8 on the DABout port on the IRF I/O.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: Driver Module, IRF I/O Board

Value: %d mA Limit: %d mA
Extended error: The driver module detected a load present on a driver that expected an open circuit because the system did not detect a coil (of the corresponding nuclei) present. If this error happens repeatedly then check for shorted load on the affected Head, Body, or MNS transmission line. Can utilize the TR DD Diagnostic to help with isolating this problem. If source of fault is MNS TR, please insure a MNS TR Switch is plugged in. If error happens intermittently and cannot be traced to failed hardware then it may be due to gradient noise in the system.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: RF Transmit Cable, Driver Module

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2253582 - EM_PEARL_DOORBELL_DP_FAILED_ACK_OF_INT_CLEAR
body:
ERROR: EM_PEARL_DOORBELL_DP_FAILED_ACK_OF_INT_CLEAR
Bridge Datapath Diagnostic - Doorbell Interrupt test failed when the master processor failed to acknowledge the interrupt was cleared by the slave processor.
Master Proc = %s
Slave Proc = %s Doorbells = 0x%08x
Poll Attempts = %d
Extended error: The interrupt was issued to the slave processor side of the Bridge module. An ISR on the slave processor should have been called when the doorbell was issued and then detected by the slave processor. The ISR clears the corresponding doorbell interrupt. Meanwhile, the master processor is polling the doorbell interrupt's status bit, checking for a cleared interrupt. After several polling attempts, the master processor failed to detect the interrupt was cleared, resulting in an error. Fault isolation is as follows:
Using a bus analyzer, verify the interrupt was issued by the master processor to the slave processor's doorbell on the Bridge module. Using a bus analyzer on the slave side of the Bridge module, verify the doorbell asserted an interrupt on the slave-side PCI bus. Also, verify the slave processor cleared the interrupt. Lastly, verify the master processor repeatedly polled the Bridge module for the cleared interrupt bit. A failure at any point will assist in fault generation (processor, communications/connectivity, or Bridge).
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: AGP Board, APS Board, Bridge Board

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2253583 - EM_PEARL_DP_FAILED_TO_COMPLETE_SLAVECMD
body:
ERROR: EM_PEARL_DP_FAILED_TO_COMPLETE_SLAVECMD
Bridge Datapath Diagnostic failed. The master processor failed to verify a function running on the slave processor successfully completed.
Master Proc = %s
Slave Proc = %s
Function = %s
Poll Attempts = %d.
Extended error: Requests to execute functions on the slave processor are initiated by the master processor using a 'slave command' interface. When called, an interface function that initiates remote execution only verifies that the function exists on the slave processor and that it can be executed. Provided those conditions are satisfied, execution of the function on the slave processor begins. The master processor verifies the function on the slave processor is done by polling the interface. This error is generated after several polling attempts failed to verify the issued command completed execution on the slave processor. Possible causes (1) issued command is still running, (2) issued command is in an endless loop,
(3) race conditions within the interface due to multiple commands being issued, or (4) problem with interface used to issued commands to the slave processor.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: Firmware

Extended error: This test verifies that the SRF(or PSE) can send data to the IRF(or IXG) over the sequence bus on the MGD backplane. This bus connects the SRF(or PSE), IRF(or IXG), and STIF(or PSEIO) boards. This test will fail if the SRF(or PSE) can not send a 32-bit parallel signal to the IRF(or IXG). The STIF(or PSEIO) is not tested by this diag but a fault on the STIF(or PSEIO) can also make this diag fail.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: SRF Board, PSE Board, IRF Board, STIF Board, PSE I/O Board, MGD Backplane

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2253619 - EM_DIAG_SRF_IRF_SEQ_CHKSUM_BAD
body:
ERROR: EM_DIAG_SRF_IRF_SEQ_CHKSUM_BAD
SRF(or PSE)->IRF(or IXG) Datapath test detected a checksum error on the sequence bus. Data on this bus is being corrupted by one of the devices hooked to the bus.
Extended error: During this test, data was sent by the SRF(or PSE) to the 32-bit sequence bus on the MDG backplane, past the STIF(or PSEIO) board, and into the IRF board. The IRF detected that the data was corrupt. This might be caused by a bad board or a bad backplane. You can isolate the effect of the STIF(or PSEIO) board by removing that board (power down first) and running the SRF(or PSE)-IRF(or IXG) diag again. The system will not run without the STIF(or PSEIO) board but the SRF(or PSE)-IRF(or IXG) diag can be run. If the test passes without the STIF(or PSEIO) the STIF(or PSEIO) is defective. Otherwise, the problem is in the SRF(or PSE), IRF(or IXG), or backplane. Check for bent packplane pins. Re-seating the IRF(or IXG)/SRF(or PSE)/STIF(or PSEIO) might help.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: SRF Board, PSE Board, PSE I/O Board, IRF Board, IXG Board, STIF Board, MGD Backplane

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2254232 - EM_RF_AST35_ERROR_0B
body:
ERROR: EM_RF_AST35_ERROR_0B
3T RF Amplifier +9 Volt Supply Low (fault 11). Possible Causes: defective power supply or excessive load. If the fault persists, replace the RF amplifier.
Extended error: The RF Amp 9 V PS is less than 8 volts. This could be due to a fuse failure, or failure of the power supply or the load in the RF Deck failed. Check Fuses F12, F13 and F14 and replace if failed. If the fuses are all functional, the open the left side interconnect panel on the RF Deck. Disconnect the 5 RF pin sub D connector, JXX. Measure for 9 V across pin 1 to pin 5. If this voltage <8 volts, replace the the power supply deck. If this voltage is >8 volts replace the the RF deck.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: RF Amp Fuse, RF Amp Power Supply, RF Amp

Extended error: The RF Amp 15 V PS is less than 14 volts. This could be due to a fuse failure, or failure of the power supply or the load in the RF Deck failed. Measure for 9 V across pin 2 to pin 5. If this voltage <14 volts, replace the the power supply deck. If this voltage is >14 volts replace the the RF deck.

body:

Extended error: The RF Amp PA Tube experienced high air temperature. Allow the RF Amp to cool for 20 minutes and restart scanning. Make sure room air temperature is <40 C, address with site if necessary. Check air filters and replace if necessary. If fault persists, replace the RF deck.

body:

Extended error: The RF Amp detected a non-fatal fault while in Standby. There are some faults like PA HV low and PA Plate Current High that can happen only when the amplifier is in Operate mode. If the controller detects these faults while in Standby mode, the RF Amp will trip with Fault 50. If this error persists, replace the the power supply deck.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: RF Amp Power Supply

title: 2254280 - EM_RF_AST35_ERROR_5F
body:

Extended error: The RF Amp RF forward power exceeded the forward power limit. Check RF Transmit Chain.
For the 35kW RF Amp, the power limit is 37.5kW in body mode and 5kW in head mode.
For the 35kW(25kW) RF Amp, the power limit is 27.5kW in body mode and 5kW in head mode.
If fault persists, replace the RF deck.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: RF Amp

Extended error: The RF Amp experienced excessive RF Reflected power. Make sure RF Transmit chain is secure and that there are no opens. If fault persists, replace the RF deck.

For the 35kW RF Amp, the limit is 2600 watts in body mode and 1000 watts in head mode.
For the 35kW(25kW) RF Amp, the limit is 1750 watts in body mode and 800 watts in head mode.
If fault persists, replace the RF deck.

ERROR: EM_RF_BB_CABLE_OFF
BB RF Amp Interface <-> BB RF Amp serial link failure.\b\ BB RF Amplifier Interface does not detect a Broadband Amplifier. Verify the cable is connected from the ASC BB IF Board to the BB Amplifier. Verify BB Amp Type matches the ASC BB IF Board Type.
Extended error: The mostly likely cause of this fault is the cable from the Spectro RF Amplifier is not connected to the ASC BB RF Amplifier Interface Board. If the cable is connected and Spectro RF Amplifier power is on, verify the Spectro RF Amplifier Type matches the type of ASC BB RF Amplifier Interface Board. There are 2 types of ASC BB RF Amplifier Interface Boards: one supports CPC type amplifiers and the other supports AMT type amplifiers. The Spectro RF Amplifier (AMT or CPC) must match the ASC BB RF Amplifier Interface Board (AMT or CPC) or the ASC BB RF Amplifier Interface Board may not detect and control the Spectro RF Amplifier properly.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2254658 - EM_DIAG_SRI_LOOP_BACK_FAIL
body:
ERROR: EM_DIAG_SRI_LOOP_BACK_FAIL
SRI Diagnostic Error. Did not get the correct data back after sending test data through the SRI communication channel. Something is corrupting the data.
Extended error: The SRI SCP loopback test should be run first. If the SRI SCP loopback test fails, replace the SCP board. If that passes, run the SRI STIF(or PSE) loopback test with a loopback cable on the STIF(or PSE) board SRI port. If this test fails verify that the loopback cable is OK and then replace the STIF(or PSE) board.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: SCP Board, STIF Board, PSE Board

Received : %d bytes.
Extended error: The SRI SCP loopback test should be run first. If the SRI SCP loopback test fails, replace the SCP board. If that passes, run the SRI STIF(or PSE) loopback test with a loopback cable on the STIF(or PSE) board SRI port. If this test fails verify that the loopback cable is OK and then replace the STIF(or PSE) board.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: SCP Board, STIF Board, PSE Board

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2257273 - EM_UPM_PREDICT_SAR_TEMP_SAR_ERROR
body:
ERROR: EM_UPM_PREDICT_SAR_TEMP_SAR_ERROR
The predicted SAR downloaded was above the temperature de-rated SAR limit. Please lower the scan room ambient temperature
Predicted SAR = %d.%d
SAR Limit = %d.%d
Scan Room Temp = %d.%d degrees C
Extended error: The SAR limits are adjusted based on the temperature read by the scan room temperature sensor. For each degree above 23.5 degrees C, the SAR limit is reduced by 0.25. If the predicted SAR of a given scan is expected to exceed the SAR limit imposed by the scan room ambient temperature, the scan will be inhibited. The most likely cause of this error is the scan room air conditioning not being set to a low enough temperature. This could also be caused by a faulty scan room air temperature sensor.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2261257 - EM_HC_RF_BB_AMP_TYPE_SDO_ERROR
body:
ERROR: EM_HC_RF_BB_AMP_TYPE_SDO_ERROR
The amplifier type of the BB RF Amp could not be read from the ASC BB IF Board. SDO Upload returned error code 0x%X.
Extended error: The SCP Board could not read the BB RF Amp type from the ASC BB IF Board. This could indicate a problem with the CAN communication between the SCP board and the ASC BB IF board. Check the CAN Communication, verify that the CAN network is terminated properly, and perform a TPS Reset to try again.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: CAN Communication, SCP Board, ASC BB IF Board

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2261258 - EM_HC_RF_BB_UNKNOWN_AMP_ID
body:
ERROR: EM_HC_RF_BB_UNKNOWN_AMP_ID
SCP received an unknown Spectro RF Amp ID from ASC BB IF Board. Verify the cable is connected from the Spectro RF Amp to the ASC BB IF Board and Spectro RF Amp Type matches ASC BB IF Board Type. Please perform a TPS Reset. Spectro RF Amp ID = 0x%02X
Extended error: An unknown RF Amp ID may mean that the RF Amp in use is not supported by the software at this time. This could also indicate a hardware problem. Check the CAN PMC board located on the SCP Board, the ASC BB IF Board, and the Spectro RF Amp. There are 2 types of ASC BB RF Amplifier Interface Boards: one supports CPC type amplifiers and the other supports AMT type amplifiers. The Spectro RF Amplifier (AMT or CPC) must match the ASC BB RF Amplifier Interface Board (AMT or CPC) or the ASC BB RF Amplifier Interface Board may not detect and control the Spectro RF Amplifier properly.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: SCP Board, ASC BB IF Board, RF Amp

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2261259 - EM_HC_RF_BB_AMP_TYPE_INCORRECT
body:
ERROR: EM_HC_RF_BB_AMP_TYPE_INCORRECT
spectroRFampType in MRconfig.cfg file does not match Spectro RF Amplifier Type determined by SCP. Please verify the RF Amp Type as well as the correct type of ASC BB IF Board is installed in the ASC. Actual ASC BB IF Board: 0x%02X - %b
Extended error: The value for the Spectro RFamp Type must match the type of BB RF Amplifier Interface Board installed in the ASC Chassis and the type of BB RF Amplifier Interface Board installed in the ASC Chassis must also match the type of Spectro RF Amplifier installed in the system. There are 2 types of ASC BB RF Amplifier Interface Boards:
one supports CPC type amplifiers and the other supports AMT type amplifiers. The actual ASC BB IF Board detected is either CPC or AMT. This type must match the Spectro RF Amplifier Type in the MRconfig.cfg for a successful TPS Reset. The Spectro RF Amplifier (AMT or CPC) must also match the ASC BB RF Amplifier Interface Board (AMT or CPC) or the ASC BB RF Amplifier Interface Board may not detect and control the Spectro RF Amplifier properly.

title: 2261738 - EM_HC_COOLING_PE_SETPOINT_OVERRANGE
body:
ERROR: EM_HC_COOLING_PE_SETPOINT_OVERRANGE
The system has detected high dew point in the PGR cabinet. Please check equipment room temperature and humidity. If in specification, contact your service representative %b
Extended error: The Aux Board (or PEM board) is communicating high temperature and humidity in the PGR cabinet. The HEC has adjusted the setpoint of the PE coolant to a maximum value of 35C to reduce the risk of condensation, but if conditions in the cabinet exceed a dewpoint of 35C, the system is at risk of condensation forming on the cold plates in the power electronics. Check that equipment room temperature and humidity are in spec, the communication between the SCP and HEC is good, and the Aux Board (or PEM board) is operating properly

title: 2267400 - EM_IRF3_DRVR_IRF3_NOT_DETECTED_ERR

Extended error: This might be caused by a momentary DVMR link dropout which might have been caused by any module connected to the DVMR fiber links. Check that the DTX is functioning and is connected to the IRF3 by a dual fiber cable. Run the DTX Board Level Diagnostics.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: NB DTx Module, IRF Board

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267404 - EM_IRF3_DRVR_RRX_CONFIRM_ERROR

Extended error: The RRX is communicating back to the IRF3 but its status indicates that it did not accept the last command value sent to from the IRF3. If this error occurs often, there is a communication fault in the IRF3, DVMR Link dual fiber cable, or RRX module.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267411 - EM_IRF3_DRVR_NO_DTX2

Extended error: Verify that the DTX2 (broadband exciter) in the penetration cabinet is powered up and connected to the IRF3 board in the CAM chassis with a dual fiber cable. The DTX2 must be connected to a clock source on the DTX1 by a clock cable.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: BB DTx Module

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267412 - EM_IRF3_DRVR_NOT_ENOUGH_RRX
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_DRVR_NOT_ENOUGH_RRX
Not enough RRX modules found. The system did not find enough RRX modules for the number of channels configured.
Extended error: The system needs 1 RRX per 16 channels. Each RRX is enumerated through its connection to the RF Hub. A bad cable between a RRX and the RF-hub, or a cable connected to the wrong jack of the RF Hub can cause the RRX to appear to be configured for the wrong set of channels and thus not counted in the required number of RRX. If the RF Hub is not powered up, the RRX connected to it will all default to channels 113 - 128.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: RRx Module, IRF Board

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267414 - EM_IRF3_DRVR_NO_XGD

NO XGD MODULE FOUND. The IRF3 board does not see the XGD module. The system must have a dual fiber cable between the GMC board (in the Cronus Chassis) of the XGD and the IRF3 board
Extended error: The IRF3 did not detect an active fiber cable from the XGD. The XGD must be connected to the IRF3 by a dual fiber cable. The XGD must have a single strand clock fiber cable from the DTX1 module. Verify that the XGD is powered on and that it's clock and data fibers are connected.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: IRF Board

title: 2267424 - EM_IRF3_DRVR_CLONED_RRX

Multiple RRX with the same ID. The IRF3 or ERF boards see one or more RRX modules with the same ID number. The system can not tell which channels to assign to each RRX.
Extended error: The RRX modules are enumerated through a cable to the RF Hub. The RF Hub must be powered up to enumerate the RRX.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: RRx Module, RF Hub Backplane

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267425 - EM_IRF3_DRVR_NO_IRF_CLOCK
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_DRVR_NO_IRF_CLOCK
No Clock Signal to IRF3 board. The IRF3 board did not detect a clock signal on the J8 fiber optic clock cable. This condition will cause a TPS_reset failure.
Extended error: The DTX1 module provides a clock signal that connects by single strand fiber to the IRF3, ERF (in systems with greater than 32 channels), XGD, and ICN modules. It also runs by coax to the TDM. The system will fail TPS reset if any of the clock inputs are disconnected.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: Mono Fiber Cable, NB DTx Module, IRF Board, ERF Board

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267426 - EM_IRF3_DRVR_IRF_IN_WRONG_SLOT
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_DRVR_IRF_IN_WRONG_SLOT
IRF3 board in wrong slot. The IRF3 board must be in slot %d of the CAM chassis. It was detected in slot %d.
Extended error: The Irf3 board must be installed in slot 11 of the MGD or slot 7 of the CAM chassis. The sequence bus runs between the SRF(or PSE) board and this slot of the chassis. The IRF3 must be in this slot to connect to the sequence bus.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: IRF Board

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267427 - EM_IRF3_DRVR_NO_ERF_CLOCK
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_DRVR_NO_ERF_CLOCK
No Clock Signal to ERF-%d board. The ERF board did not detect a clock signal on the J8 fiber optic clock cable. This condition will cause a TPS_reset failure.
Extended error: The DTX1 module provides a clock signal that connects by single strand fiber to the IRF3, ERF, XGD, and ICN modules. It also runs by coax to the TDM. The system will fail TPS reset if any of the clock inputs are disconnected.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: Mono Fiber Cable, NB DTx Module, IRF Board, ERF Board

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267428 - EM_IRF3_DRVR_BAD_IRF3_LINK
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_DRVR_BAD_IRF3_LINK
Bad fiber link(s) on IRF3 board. A bad dual fiber connected to the Irf3 board is preventing any of the links from working. One or more remote modules are powered up but not communicating over its dual fiber link.
Extended error: This is most likely a problem with a 80MHz reference clock signal to one or more external modules. The ICNs, XGD and ERFs (in systems with more than 32 channels) get there ref clock signals over a single strand fiber from the DTX1 module. The RRX get their ref clock signal through a twin-ax cable running from the DTX1 to the TDM module on the side of the magnet. Verify that the DTX module power LED is lit. Verify that a very dim red light present on J20-J23 of the DTX1. Verify that DTX2 (in systems with MNS) is connected to DTX1 by a 9-pin cable hooked to J14. Check the status of the device connected to the indicated port. Verify that this device has a 80MHz clock reference signal from the DTX1.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: Mono Fiber Cable, Dual Fiber Module, NB DTx Module, Transient Detection Module, IRF Board, RRx Module

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267429 - EM_IRF3_DRVR_BAD_ERF_LINK
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_DRVR_BAD_ERF_LINK
Bad fiber link(s) on ERF-%d board. A bad fiber connected to the ERF board is preventing any of the links from working. One or more remote RRX modules are powered up but not communicating over its fiber link.
Extended error: If any module connected to the IRF or ERF is powered up but not functioning that device will prevent all the other devices from communicating over fiber. Check the status of the device connected to the indicated port. Verify that the device has a 80MHz clock reference signal.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: Mono Fiber Cable, Dual Fiber Module, NB DTx Module, IRF Board, ERF Board, RRx Module

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267430 - EM_IRF3_DRVR_BAD_CENTER_FREQ
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_DRVR_BAD_CENTER_FREQ
Bad Center Frequency Requested. The DTX-%d module was commanded to a center freq of %d Hz. The module is limited to %d to %d Hz. This is a software error.
Extended error: The DTX come in 1.5T, 3T, and MNS versions. Each type can only handle a limited range of output frequencies. Software or configuration errors may cause the system to request a frequency that is beyond the limit of the hardware. Verify you have the right type of DTX and the fieldStrength entry in Guided_Install is correct.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: NB DTx Module, BB DTx Module

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267431 - EM_IRF3_NOT_READY_IRF_INIT
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_NOT_READY_IRF_INIT
The IRF3 is not ready.
Extended error: This is just a warning message that indicates that another error message has already been logged about a serious problem with the IRF3, DTX, RRX, TDM, interconnect cable, or other error that is preventing the system from controlling the exciters and receivers. Look for a previous error message about configuration errors, cable errors, module errors, or calibration errors. Scans will not be allowed until that problem is corrected

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267432 - EM_IRF3_NOT_READY_REF_CLK
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_NOT_READY_REF_CLK
The Reference Clock to the IRF3 or ERF is not present.
Extended error: The DTX1 exciter module is not providing a 80MHz clock signal via fiber to the IRF3 board. Verify that the DTX1 is powered up and has a single strand fiber cable running to the J8 of the IRF3 board.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267433 - EM_IRF3_NOT_READY_IRD_LINKS
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_NOT_READY_IRD_LINKS
The Receiver, Exciter, or Gradient fiber communication links are not ready.
Extended error: One or more of the fiber links between the IRF3 and the RRX, Exciter, and XGD are not active. The system requires active links to all of these devices before a scan can be started.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267434 - EM_IRF3_NOT_READY_VRF_LINKS
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_NOT_READY_VRF_LINKS
The Receiver to Recon Engine fiber links are not ready.
Extended error: The dual fiber links between the RRX module located on the side of the magnet and VRE are not in the correct state. Check that the dual link fibers are connected correctly and that the VRE's have an active clock fiber attached. Look for fiber link error messages reported from the VRE.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267435 - EM_IRF3_NOT_READY_2ND_SOA
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_NOT_READY_2ND_SOA
A PSD error put the RRX into an error state. A 2nd Start Of Acquisition arrived before the current view completed.
Extended error: This error indicates that the RRX saw a 2nd SOA (StartOfAcquisition) before it had completed collecting the previous view. This event causes the RRX to produce a bad frame of data which requires the scan to be aborted. If this problem is seen often in the same scan type, the cause is probably a timing problem in the PSD.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267436 - EM_IRF3_IRDS_WERE_CLEARED
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_IRDS_WERE_CLEARED
The AGP detected a fault on the fibers connected to the IRF3 board. If a scan was running it was stopped. The system will try to recover. If no further errors are detected the system will allow scans to resume.
Extended error: The control registers of the RRX or Exciter were found to be cleared. This indicates they were reset probably by a glitch in the fiber network. A problem with any device on the fiber network can cause all devices on the fiber network to soft-reset themselves.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267437 - EM_IRF3_RRX_VRE_CABLES_REVERSED
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_RRX_VRE_CABLES_REVERSED
Fiber connector J4 of RRX-%d is not connected to a VRE. J4 must be connected to VRE and J5 goes to the IRF3 or ERF boards.
Extended error: The IRF3 board in the CAM chassis did not detect a VRE connected to the J4 connector of this RRX module. Verify that the two fiber cables in this RRX are not reversed.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267438 - EM_IRF3_FIBER_NOT_ACTIVE
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_FIBER_NOT_ACTIVE
The fiber connected to %s J%d does not have an active signal. This indicates that the module on the other side of that fiber does not have a 80MHz clock reference signal or is defective.
Extended error: If any module connected to the IRF or ERF is powered up but not functioning that device will prevent all the other devices from communicating over fiber. Check the status of the device connected to the indicated port. Verify that the device has a 80MHz clock reference signal. Check for other errors in log that reference a missing 80MHz clock. The 80MHz clock arrives from DTX1 on single strand fiber optic cable.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: Dual Fiber Module

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267439 - EM_IRF3_TOO_MANY_DTX
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_TOO_MANY_DTX
The system detected more than one identical exciter connected to the IRF3. The system may at most one NB Exciter and one BB Exciter.
Extended error: The system detected multiple exciters that all have the same instance ID. This can be cause by a defective module reporting the wrong device ID or by actually hooking up two identical exciters.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: NB DTx Module

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267440 - EM_IRF3_BAD_DTX_ID
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_BAD_DTX_ID
The system detected an exciter with an illegal instance ID. more than one identical exciter connected to the IRF3.
Extended error: The system detected an exciters whose instance ID is not 0 or 1. This can be cause by a defective reporting the wrong device ID.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: NB DTx Module

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267441 - EM_IRF3_VRF_HOOKED_TO_IRF
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_VRF_HOOKED_TO_IRF
The system detected an ICN hooked to the IRF3. Each ICN must be hooked to J4 of a RRX module.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267442 - EM_IRF3_DRVR_IRFIO_NOT_DETECTED_ERR
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_DRVR_IRFIO_NOT_DETECTED_ERR
The IRF_IO board was not found in the CAM chassis.
Extended error: The IRF_IO board must be in the slot directly behind the IRF3 board.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: IRF I/O Board

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267443 - EM_IRF3_DIAGS_MNS_NUCLEI_SELECT
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_DIAGS_MNS_NUCLEI_SELECT
DTX2 could not set its MNS nuclei select register. %d of %d values failed.
Extended error: The broadband exciter was not able to program the MNS nuclei select regsiter internal to that module. This is an error internal to the DTX-2.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: BB DTx Module

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267444 - EM_IRF3_DIAGS_RRX_BLD_SKIP
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_DIAGS_RRX_BLD_SKIP
The RRX BLD diags were halted early due to cabling or signal errors that have already been reported in this log. No RRX BLD log file was generated.
Extended error: The filter analysis portion of RRX BLD was skipped due to errors that have already been logged. Check this log for recently logged errors and correct the reported issues.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: RRx Module

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267445 - EM_IRF3_SEQ_BUS_DEAD
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_SEQ_BUS_DEAD
The IRF board is not receiving data from the Sequencer board over the sequence bus. The system can not scan until the Sequencer board returns to normal mode.
Extended error: The SRF(or PSE) normally never stops sending data to the IRF/IXG over the sequence bus. Run SRF and TRF (or PSE) diagnostics. Run SRF(or PSE) to IRF/IXG DP diagnostics to test the sequence bus that runs from the SRF(or PSE) to the IRF/IXG over the backplane.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: SRF Board, PSE Board, IRF Board, IXG Board

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267446 - EM_IRF3_LINK_INIT_TIMEOUT
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_LINK_INIT_TIMEOUT
The %s module did not send a Fiber Link Init Complete message to the AGP within the required time. Therefore AGP has forced a TPS_Reset fail and has aborted DTX and RRX calibration routines.
Extended error: Look for error messages about the module that did not complete fiber link initialization within the required time. An internal error may be preventing that module from communicating with the AGP.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267447 - EM_IRF3_SEQ_BUS_CHKSUM_ERRS
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_SEQ_BUS_CHKSUM_ERRS
The IRF3 or IXG board found sequence bus checksum errors during the last scan. The error count was %d for the scan.
Extended error: The sequence bus runs across the CAM backplane from the SRF(or PSE) board to the IRF3 or IXG board. 1,000,000 data packets flow over this bus every 4 seconds. The reported error count is how many of those packets had checksum errors during the last scan. Sequence bus errors might cause scan defects. Try running the SRF to IRF3 (or PSE to IXG) datapath diag to check for hardware defects.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: SRF Board, IRF Board, IXG Board

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267448 - EM_IRF3_WRONG_DTX_REV
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_WRONG_DTX_REV
The DTX%d module is not the correct revision required by this system. Found DTX module FPGA rev 0x%02X but need rev 0x%02X or higher. This problem will force TPS reset to fail.
Extended error: The DTX (exciter) module needs to be replaced with the correct revision of the DTX.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: NB DTx Module

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267500 - EM_IRF3_RRX_CAL_ZERO_OFF_OVER
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_RRX_CAL_ZERO_OFF_OVER
RRX Zero DC Offset Failure One or more channels on the RRX module(s) sees a DC offset that is too large to compensate for. The file /usr/g/service/log/rrxZeroOffset<date>.log has details on which RRX modules have the DC offset overrange.
Extended error: The RRX hardware can compensate for a DC offset in the range +/-127. This offset is a DC level seen by the ADC chips that originates on the RRX circuit board or in the ADC chip itself. If the RRX module consistently fails this calibration, it should be replaced.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: RRx Module

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267501 - EM_IRF3_RRX_CAL_ZERO_OFF_NO_DATA
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_RRX_CAL_ZERO_OFF_NO_DATA
RRX Zero Offset Data Collection Failure One or more channels on the RRX module(s) could not be read. The file /usr/g/service/log/rrxZeroOffset<date>.log has details on which RRX modules had this problem.
Extended error: The RRX hardware can compensate for a DC offset in the range +/-127. The RRX channels are blanked and sample data is returned to the IRF3. This calibration function did not get data for one or more of the channels.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: RRx Module

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267502 - EM_IRF3_DTX_CAL_LOW_SIGNAL
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_DTX_CAL_LOW_SIGNAL
Low signal during DTX%d calibration DTX calibration was aborted because the measured full strength signal was
too low. Expected signal level: %d, Actual level: %d
Extended error: With the DTX set to full gain, the measured signal level was too low. This signal is sent from the DTX to the RF Hub which loops it back to all the RRX input channels. A low signal can be caused by a bad DTX, a bad or disconnected cable, a defect in the RF Hub, or a bad RRX.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: NB DTx Module, RRx Module

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267503 - EM_IRF3_DTX_CAL_NO_DATA
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_DTX_CAL_NO_DATA
DTX%d Calibration Data Collection Failure Calibration of the DTX%d failed because the Irf3 could not collect sample data from the 1st RRX module. This could be a communication failure or an analog signal so large it overflowed the RRX.
Extended error: DTX calibration uses the Irf3 board to collect sample data from the 1st RRX module. The DTX calibration failed because the data collection from the RRX failed at least one time. This could indicate a problem with the RRX, the Irf3, or the clock and data fiber cables that connect these devices together.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: RRx Module, RF Hub Switch Board, RF Hub Control Board, IRF Board

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267504 - EM_IRF3_DTX_VAL_FAILURE
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_DTX_VAL_FAILURE
DTX%d Calibration is out of range. DTX calibration failed to obtain accurate results. The file /usr/g/service/log/dtx%d_val_I_<date>.log has details.
Extended error: DTX calibration calculates HW settings that allows the system to set TG from 0.0 to 39.9dB with an accuracy of +/- 0.1dB. This diag found that one or more points measured outside of the required accuracy. This may be due to excessive noise in the system or a bad DTX.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: NB DTx Module, RRx Module

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267505 - EM_IRF3_RFHUB_LOOPBACK_TIMEOUT
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_RFHUB_LOOPBACK_TIMEOUT
AGP requested SCP to %s RF Hub loop-back mode but AGP did not get a reply from SCP. Look for RF Hub related errors logged by the SCP.
Extended error: DTX and RRX calibration use RF Hub loop-back to route DTX signals to the RRX. The RF Hub failed to respond to a loop-back command in time. This may be due to the RF Hub being off-line or a problem with CAN cables to the RF Hub. Run RF Hub diagnostics to isolate the cause.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267506 - EM_IRF3_RFHUB_LOOPBACK_FAIL

Extended error: DTX and RRX calibration use RF Hub loop-back to route DTX signals to the RRX. The RF Hub responded to a loop-back command with a failure indication. This may be caused by a failure within the RF Hub. Run RF Hub diagnostics to isolate the cause.

Extended error: DTX and RRX calibration use RF Hub loop-back to route DTX signals to the RRX. The RF Hub will go into a sleep state after being commanded to loop-back mode and should not wake-up until commanded out of loop-back. Run RF Hub diagnostics to isolate the cause.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267512 - EM_IRF3_RRXCAL_FAILURE

ERROR: EM_IRF3_RRXCAL_FAILURE
The Receiver Gain Calibration on the VRE failed on R1 step %d. The file /usr/g/service/log/r1GainCal_<date>.dat has information on which receiver channel and R1 step had this problem.
Extended error: The calibration produces dB gain values that are checked against tolerances. Either a cal result exceeded its tolerance or the nominal magnitude used in the calculation was zero.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)

The Receiver Gain Calibration does not currently support FFT type processing. The VRE was commanded to calibrate using FFT processing which is not supported. This is a software error.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: Software

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267514 - EM_IRF3_RFCAL_FAILED_LOOPBACK
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_RFCAL_FAILED_LOOPBACK
The %s calibration was aborted because the RF Hub could not be put into loopback mode. Look for previous errors regarding RF Hub control.
Extended error: During calibration, the AGP asks the SCP to put the RF Hub into loopback mode by sending it commands over the CAN network. The problem could be with the SCP control of the Hub over CAN or there could be an error condition that prevents the Hub from being put into sleep mode.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267515 - EM_IRF3_RRXCAL_WARNING_DATA
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_RRXCAL_WARNING_DATA
The R1 gain calibration passed but is very close to the spec limit. This message is a warning that TPS reset may fail in the future if the R1 gain steps drift past their spec limits. R1 Step : %d
Extended error: The R1 gain calibration reports that it sees a R1 gain value that is almost out of spec. The system measures each of 13 R1 gain values for each channel and compares them to an accepted range. This system is right at that limit. The attenuators on the RF Hub switch boards that control these gain values are not adjustable. This warning will not prevent scanning but if the R1 gain measurements get worse, scanning will be blocked. View the log file /usr/g/service/log/r1GainCal_<date>.dat for the signal levels seen on each channel for each of the 13 R1 attenuation steps. This calibration sends a signal from DTX1 to the RF Hub to the RRX. The R1 attenuators are located on the switch boards of the RF Hub.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: RRx Module, RF Hub Switch Board

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267518 - EM_IRF3_RFCAL_RFHUB_ABORT
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_RFCAL_RFHUB_ABORT
Calibrations were aborted because the RF Hub will not stay in loop-back mode. Some condition is causing the RH-Hub to constantly wake up from its sleep state.
Extended error: DTX and RRX calibration use RF Hub loop-back to route DTX signals to the RRX. The RF Hub will go into a sleep state after being commanded to loop-back mode and should not wake-up until commanded out of loop-back. Run RF Hub diagnostics to isolate the cause.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267519 - EM_IRF3_RFCAL_RFHUB_ERRORS
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_RFCAL_RFHUB_ERRORS
Calibrations were aborted because the RF Hub reported error conditions related to receiver or exciters cables or power supplies.
Extended error: The RF Hub monitors the status of the multiple items related to the RRX and the loopback signal from the exciters. All of these signals must be in a good state before calibration can proceed. Correct the errors reported in the previous error messages before running RF calibration diagnostics again. (where RF Calibration is the exciter and receiver calibration - not calibration of the external RF Amp.)

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267520 - EM_IRF3_R1CAL_MIN_SIGNAL
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_R1CAL_MIN_SIGNAL
The R1 gain calibration failed because the signal was received at the RRX for one or more channels was too small. This will cause TPS_reset to fail.
Extended error: The R1 gain calibration reports that it sees a much smaller than expected signal on one or more channels. The error message just reports the first bad channel seen. There may be others too. View the log file /usr/g/service/log/r1GainCal_<date>.dat for the signal levels seen on each channel for each of the 13 R1 attenuation steps. This calibration sends a signal from DTX1 to the RF Hub to the RRX. The R1 attenuators are located on the switch boards of the RF Hub.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: RRx Module, RF Hub Switch Board

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267521 - EM_IRF3_R1CAL_GAIN_LEVEL_ERROR
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_R1CAL_GAIN_LEVEL_ERROR
The R1 gain calibration failed because one or more channels are out of spec. This error will cause a TPS reset failure. See the file /usr/g/service/log/r1GainCal_<date>.dat.
Extended error: The R1 gain calibration reports that it sees a R1 gain value that is out of spec. The system measures each of 13 R1 gain values for each channel and compares them to an accepted range. The attenuators on the RF Hub switch boards that control these gain values are not adjustable. There may be additional channels and R1 steps that are bad. This error just reports the first one seen. View the log file /usr/g/service/log/r1GainCal_<date>.dat for the signal levels seen on each channel for each of the 13 R1 attenuation steps. This calibration sends a signal from DTX1 to the RF Hub to the RRX. The R1 attenuators are located on the switch boards of the RF Hub.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: RRx Module, RF Hub Switch Board

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267522 - EM_IRF3_EXCESSIVE_RFHUB_WAKEUP
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_EXCESSIVE_RFHUB_WAKEUP
The DTX or RRX calibration was aborted after multiple attempts because the RF Hub would not stay in loopback mode.
Extended error: DTX and RRX calibration use RF Hub loop-back to route DTX signals to the RRX. The RF Hub will go into a sleep state after being commanded to loop-back mode and should not wake-up until commanded out of loop-back. There are multiple reasons that will cause the RF Hub to come out of sleep mode unexpectedly. Run RF Hub related diagnostics to isolate the cause.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: RF Hub Control Board, RRx Module

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267523 - EM_IRF3_PERSISTANT_DVMR_LINK_DROPOUT
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_PERSISTANT_DVMR_LINK_DROPOUT
The DTX or RRX calibration was aborted after multiple attempts because the DVMR dual fiber links are failing. This will cause TPS_reset to fail.
Extended error: The dual fiber links between the IRF3 and the DTX, RRX, and XGD, and the fiber links between the RRX and the ICNs are not staying active. The system aborted the current action because these fiber links could not be successfully reinitialized. Verify that all of the fiber cables are firmly locked in their sockets. Verify that the fiber cables have not been crimped or damaged. Check operation of SFP fiber optic xcvr modules on both ends of link. Look for an error message in the system error log identifying which module caused the DVMR fiber network to fail.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: Dual Fiber Module, NB DTx Module, RRx Module, Dual Fiber Cable

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)

Extended error: The IRF board should be able to acquire the local clock. Failure to to acquire the local clock indicates a problem with the IRF board.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: IRF Board

title: 2267597 - EM_IRF3_DRVR_NO_RRX
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_DRVR_NO_RRX
The RRX_%d module was not detected by IRF3. The system can not scan without this module.
Extended error: The system needs 1 RRX per 16 channels. Each RRX is enumerated through its connection to the RF Hub. A bad cable between a RRX and the RF-hub or a RF Hub switch board in the wrong slot can cause the RRX to appear to be configured for the wrong set of channels and thus not counted in the required number of RRX. If the RF Hub is not powered up, the RRX connected to it will all default to channels 113 - 128.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: RRx Module, Dual Fiber Cable, Dual Fiber Module

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267600 - EM_IRF3_FIRST_LINK_DOWN
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_FIRST_LINK_DOWN
The IRF3 detected a fault on the fiber links. Status register=0x%X The modules connected to these IRF3 jacks were determined to be the cause of
the disruption: %s
Extended error: A momentary problem with any module connected to the DVMR dual fiber links can bring the links down for every node. The IRF3 can detect which link was the first to drop out. The module connected to that link should be the one who initiated the problem. If several modules dropped out at the same time the IRF3 will report multiple modules. In this case there might be a single problem effecting multiple modules such as a power supply glitch or a drop out on the shared reference clock source. Note: a problem on the RRX to ICN links will cause the RRX to IRF3 link to go down so errors reported against the RRX may be caused by a problem with an ICN.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: Dual Fiber Cable, Mono Fiber Cable, Dual Fiber Module, RRx Module, NB DTx Module, Img Compute Node, IRF Board, Transient Detection Module

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267604 - EM_IRF3_DTX_RRX_GAIN_LEVEL
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_DTX_RRX_GAIN_LEVEL
The Exciter to Receiver datapath diag found that the difference in signal levels between receiver channels was to great. Examine this file for more information: /usr/g/service/log/dtxRrx_loopback_<date>.log
Extended error: This diag send a signal from the Exciter through the RF Hub to all the receiver channels. The receivers should see the same signal on all channels with an amplitude that is within +/- 1.5dB from the average for all channels. This error will aslo be generated if the average signal level is too low. Large differences in per-channel gains might be caused by a bad Rf Hub switch board, bad receiver module, or possibly a bad Rf Hub control board. Run the RRX BLDs to verify that the RRX are working correctly. Run the RF Hub BLDs to verify the RF Hub status.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: RF Hub Switch Board, RRx Module, RF Hub Control Board

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267605 - EM_IRF3_DTX_RRX_RF_FILTER
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_DTX_RRX_RF_FILTER
The Exciter to Receiver datapath diag found filter response errors that might be caused by the Exciter, the RF Hub switch boards, or the receiver module. Examine this file for more information:
/usr/g/service/log/dtxRrx_loopback_<date>.log
Extended error: This diag send a signal from the Exciter through the RF Hub to all the receiver channels. The diagnostic measures SNR levels and filter frequency response for all of these devices. If a measured response is outside of the allowed margins, this diagnostic cannot isolate FRU. Examine the log file for items that are marked as failed. A failure that occurs on all channels for one of the sub-tests was probably caused by a bad exciter. A failure that only effects a group of 16 channels was probably caused by a bad receiver or Rf Hub switch board.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: RF Hub Switch Board, RRx Module, NB DTx Module

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267606 - EM_IRF_RRX_LINK_ERRS
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF_RRX_LINK_ERRS
Link errors were seen on the Receiver module %d to IRF3 fiber link.
Missing data packets: %d
Invalid data packets: %d
Uncorrected data packets reported by IRF3: %d Uncorrected data packets reported by receiver: %d
Extended error: The IRF3 and Receiver hardware counts the number of corrupted or missing packets seen on the fiber links. The counters are cleared at the beginning of a scan and read at the end of a scan. Each link error provides a small chance important control or status data was lost during the scan. The likelihood of observable system errors increases with the frequency of link errors. These errors can be caused by bad clock single strand fibers, bad DVMR Link dual fibers, a defective clock module in the exciter, a defective receiver module or a defective IRF3 board.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: Dual Fiber Module, Dual Fiber Cable, RRx Module, IRF Board

Confirm VRF Link Up LED located on top of RRx is brightly illuminated.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: Img Compute Node, RRx Module, Dual Fiber Cable, Dual Fiber Module

title: 2267620 - EM_IRF3_DTX_RRX_MNS_RF_FILTER
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_DTX_RRX_MNS_RF_FILTER
The Exciter to Receiver datapath diag found filter response errors that might be caused by the MNS Exciter, the RF Hub switch boards, or the receiver module. Examine this file for more information:
/usr/g/service/log/dtxRrx_MNS_loopback_<date>.log
Extended error: This diag send a signal from the MNS Exciter (DTX-2) through the upconverter to the RF Hub switch boards and on to the receiver modules. The diagnostic measures SNR levels and filter frequency response for all of these devices. If a measured response is outside of the allowed margins, this diagnostic cannot isolate FRU. Examine the log file for items that are marked as failed. A failure that occurs on all channels for one of the sub-tests was probably caused by a bad exciter. A failure that only effects a group of 8 channels was probably caused by a bad upconverter, receiver or Rf Hub switch board.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: RF Hub Switch Board, RRx Module, NB DTx Module

title: 2267621 - EM_IRF3_DTX_RRX_MNS_GAIN_LEVEL
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_DTX_RRX_MNS_GAIN_LEVEL
The Exciter to Receiver datapath diag found that the difference in signal levels between receiver channels was to great. Examine this file for more information: /usr/g/service/log/dtxRrx_MNS_loopback_<date>.log
Extended error: This diag send a signal from the MNS Exciter (DTX-2) to the upconverter, then to the RF Hub switch boards and on to the receiver modules. The receivers should see the same signal on all channels with an amplitude that is within +/- 1.5dB from the average for all channels. This error will aslo be generated if the average signal level is too low. Large differences in per-channel gains might be caused by a bad Rf Hub switch board, bad receiver module, or possibly a bad Rf Hub control board. Run the RRX BLDs to verify that the RRX are working correctly. Run the RF Hub BLDs to verify the RF Hub status.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: RF Hub Switch Board, RRx Module, RF Hub Control Board

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267623 - EM_IRF3_TNS_COUNT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_TNS_COUNT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED
During the last scan, the system suppressed an unusually large number of transient noise events. %d TNS counts were detected. Check scan room doors, call service if this condition persists.
Extended error: When the TDM detects noise in the scan room larger than the preset threshold value, the TDM commands the receivers to ignore the analog input signals and just send zeros in their digital outputs. This reduces the impact of a noise spike on the output image but still degrades the image somewhat. This error message indicates that the system detected an unusually large amount of noise during the previous scan. Check the scan room door seals and for other sources of noise inside the scan room such as: loose metal on metal contact of fasteners and hardware, incandescent bulbs with noisy filaments, fluorescent lighting, and 3rd-party electronic devices. Use the EPI White Pixel Test or Spike Noise Triangulation tool to locate the noise sources.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: Transient Detection Module

title: 2267636 - EM_IRF3_DIAG_ABORT_LINKS_NOT_READY
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_DIAG_ABORT_LINKS_NOT_READY
This diagnostic was aborted because the IRF3/IXG is currently not communicating with all the DTX, RRX, XGD, and ICN modules that are required for the current system configuration. The communication problem must be corrected before this diag can run.
Extended error: The system has a problem with the fiber links between the IRF3/IXG board and the various modules that connect to those fibers. The diag that was aborted is a higher-level diag that is not useful for diagnosing the communication problem. Examine the error messages logged during TPS reset or run lower-level diags such as IRF3_BLD to diagnose the fiber link problems. DVMR fiber link problems can be caused by bad fibers, bad fiber modules, or any device connected to the fiber network including ICN, IRF3 or IXG, DTX, RRX, or XGD.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: IRF Board, RRx Module, NB DTx Module, Img Compute Node, IXG Board

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2267637 - EM_IRF3_FIRST_LINK_DOWN_R2
body:
ERROR: EM_IRF3_FIRST_LINK_DOWN_R2
AGP detected a fault on the fiber links connected to IRF3 or IXG or ERF.
The link to this device dropped out: %s
Extended error: A momentary problem with any module connected to the DVMR dual fiber links can bring the links down for every node. The IRF3 can detect which link was the first to drop out. The module connected to that link should be the one who initiated the problem. If several modules dropped out at the same time the IRF3 will report multiple modules. In this case there might be a single problem effecting multiple modules such as a power supply glitch or a drop out on the shared reference clock source. Note: a problem on the RRX to ICN links will cause the RRX to IRF3 link to go down so errors reported against the RRX may be caused by a problem with an ICN.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: RRx Module, NB DTx Module, Img Compute Node, IRF Board, IXG Board, Dual Fiber Cable, Mono Fiber Cable, Transient Detection Module, ERF Board

AGP detected that the XG2 function on the IXG board stopped communicating with the IRF3 function on the IXG board. This indicates a problem with the gradient subsystem
Extended error: In this system the IRF3 and XG2 processor are both located on the IXG board. This error message indicates that the communication link between the two devices on the IXG stopped unexpectedly. If this happens during a scan, the scan must be stopped. The most likely cause for this event is that the XG2 detected an error condition in the gradients and reset itself to get to a safe state. Check for faults in the gradient system.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: IXG Board

Extended error: If no XGD specific faults are available, try the following steps:
* Verify that the 420 volt circuit breaker on the PDU is on.
* Verify that the DVMR link fiberoptic cable form the IRF3(or IXG) is connected to the GMC DVMR link transceiver in XGD.
* Verify that the IRF3(or IXG) and GMC DVMR link transeivers are operational.
* Verify that the DVMR link cable from IRF3(or IXG) to the GMC is not damaged.
* Verify that the transeiver from the exciter to the GMC clock input is good.
* Verify that the clock fiberoptic cable form the exiter to the GMC is good.
* Power down the XGD and verify that the GMC, XGA-CB and XPS-CB boards are seated securely in their slots by removing and re-seating each board. Power on the XGD and perform a TPS reset.
* Power down the MGD chassis and verify that IRF3(or IXG) is seated securely in its slot by removing and re-seating it. Power on the MGD chassis and perform a TPS reset.

title: 2267825 - EM_XGD_ESTOP_BUTTON_PRESSED
body:
ERROR: EM_XGD_ESTOP_BUTTON_PRESSED
The emergency stop button has been pressed or the emergency stop cable has been disconnected.
Extended error: This message may also result from a low voltage condition on the 48v supply. To recover, press the EMO Reset button. You will have to move the SRI to the home position and re-landmark before scanning. If after EMO Reset XGA, XRFD, and Pen Cabinet are still without power then reference E-Stop block diagram and check for open circuit somewhere in E-Stop loop. If after EMO Reset XRFD and Pen Cabinet are receiving power but ENABLE and HEARTBEAT LEDs on all XGA units are dark, reference PDU block diagram and check operation of 48V PS2 supply inside PDU. If after EMO Reset XGA, XRFD, and Pen Cabinet all have power but system still reports E-Stop, confirm all cable connections to Auxiliary Board.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2268225 - EM_PDU_INT_FAIL
body:
ERROR: EM_PDU_INT_FAIL
The Aux Board is reporting a distortion of one or more of the incoming AC line phases to the PDU or a 48V undervoltage event.
Extended error: Check for messages reported at same time describing 48V undervoltage or overvoltage events. If undervoltage or overvoltage events reported confirm Cronus GMC Chassis boards and Auxiliary Module, which receive PS1 power, show active power LED indicators. If power LEDs inactive then cycle Gradient 48V Control circuit breaker on front of PDU. If cycling required or if LEDs are OK but undervoltage and overvoltage messages are seen then the 48V PDU PS1 power supply is exhibiting degraded performance. Replace at next earliest convenience. If LEDs are OK and no undervoltage or overvoltage messages seen then check quality of each incoming power line phase to PDU.

title: 2268937 - EM_SRI_CAN_ADV2SCAN_LOCKOUT
body:
ERROR: EM_SRI_CAN_ADV2SCAN_LOCKOUT
Advance to scan attempted while locked out for workflow efficiency. See in-room display for next step to perform.
Extended error: This message indicates that the operator attempted an advance to scan operation while locked out by the host. This typically happens when the host is waiting for the user to perform a different workflow operation, such as identifying the location of floating coils.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2268939 - EM_SRI_CAN_TNG_CABLE_MISSING
body:
ERROR: EM_SRI_CAN_TNG_CABLE_MISSING
The SRI did not detect the touch-and-go landmark cable. Call for service.
Extended error: The SRI did not detect the touch-and-go landmark cable between the SRI and the electrical dock. Confirm this cable is connected and the SRI is operating correctly. Execute the SRI Functional (Touch-N-Go) diagnostic to confirm the operation once the problem is corrected

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2268940 - EM_SRI_CAN_SAR_LIMIT_GETSTATE
body:
ERROR: EM_SRI_CAN_SAR_LIMIT_GETSTATE
Firmware error: The SRI was unable to read the expected SAR from the UPM. The bore fan will be set to high-speed during scanning until the problem is resolved.
Extended error: This error is logged if the SRI firmware on the SCP is unable to read the expected SAR value from the UPM firmware on the SCP. When this occurs, the SRI will set the bore fan speed to high-speed for all scans regardless of the expected SAR. This problem can be caused by a failure of the UPM firmware on the SCP to initialize. Look earlier in the log for other errors that may have occurred first. Execute the CAN link diagnostic and the UPM diagnostic to help isolate the problem.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2269055 - EM_DIAG_1WIRE_NBPIO_FIBER_LINK

This may be reported when other devices on the DVMR Fiber Optic Link are down. Verify the Exciter 80MHz Clock (a single Fiber Optic cable) is connected to the IRF3 Board.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2269108 - EM_DIAG_1WIRE_TDM_POWER
body:
ERROR: EM_DIAG_1WIRE_TDM_POWER
The regulated TDM internal voltages are out of specification.
Extended error: Verify that the SRPS is outputting the correct voltages. This message will be logged if error message 2269107 is logged indicating the input voltage to the TDM is not correct. If the input voltage is correct and the SRPS voltages are correct, this may be caused by a defective voltage regulator in the TDM or a TDM wiring error.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: Transient Detection Module

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2269109 - EM_DIAG_1WIRE_TDM_CLKIN
body:
ERROR: EM_DIAG_1WIRE_TDM_CLKIN
The TDM does not have a clock reference input signal. Verify that the exciter/clock ref module is powered up and that the twin-ax cable is connected from the exciter to TDM module.
Extended error: The 80MHz clock reference signal is generated by the exciter and sent to the TDM over a twin-ax cable. The TDM distributes this clock signal to each of the RRX modules. Verify that the clock ref cable and the LO cable are not swapped on the exciter side. Verify that the two pins on each end of the twin-ax cable are not damaged.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: NB DTx Module

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2269110 - EM_DIAG_1WIRE_TDM_CLKOUT
body:
ERROR: EM_DIAG_1WIRE_TDM_CLKOUT
The TDM did not detect the 80MHz clock reference at the TDM outputs to the RRX modules.
Extended error: If the TDM detects a reference clock at its input from the exciter but not at its output to the RRX, then the TDM may have an internal fault.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: Transient Detection Module

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2269111 - EM_DIAG_1WIRE_TDM_ANTENNA
body:
ERROR: EM_DIAG_1WIRE_TDM_ANTENNA
The TNS antenna is not connected to the TDM.
Extended error: Reconnect the TNS loop antenna to the TDM on the side of the magnet. If connected, then check the cable connected at the TDM all the way to the loop antenna. Verify the TNS loop antenna is not damaged with a defective solder joint or a broken center wire at the antenna.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2269112 - EM_DIAG_1WIRE_BBPIO_CLOCK
body:
ERROR: EM_DIAG_1WIRE_BBPIO_CLOCK
The 1-Wire device in the MNS Exciter is not detecting the 80MHz clock ref signal from the NB Exciter.
Extended error: If other devices (TDM, Exciter and IRF3) are also reporting a missing exciter clock reference signal, check MNS Exciter and NB Exciter power.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: BB DTx Module, NB DTx Module

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2269113 - EM_DIAG_1WIRE_BBPIO_FIBER_LINK
body:
ERROR: EM_DIAG_1WIRE_BBPIO_FIBER_LINK
The 1-Wire Network did not detect communication on the DVMR Fiber Optic Link between the MNS Exciter and the IRF3 Board.
Extended error: Verify that a DVMR Fiber Optic Link is connected securely between the MNS exciter and the IRF3 or IXG board in the CAM chassis. Verify that the clock cable is connected between the narrowband and MNS exciters. Verify that both exciters have power. Verify that the Clk Ref LED on the IRF3 or IXG board is on and not blinking. Its possible for failures in other modules (exciters, receivers, VRE, or XGD) to prevent this module from establishing a link over its DVMR Fiber Optic Link.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2269116 - EM_DIAG_1WIRE_SRPS_FAULT_RESET
body:
ERROR: EM_DIAG_1WIRE_SRPS_FAULT_RESET
The 1-Wire Network indicates that the SRPS has faulted. The system was not able to clear this fault by itself. Manual SRPS recovery is necessary.
Extended error: If the SRPS is currently faulted, the fault LED in its front panel will be lighted. The system will automatically try to reset a faulted SRPS but won't try more than two times. If the 2nd SRPS reset attempt does not clear the fault, manual intervention is required. Run 1-wire diagnostics to see the current state of the individual SRPS fault and warning signals. Power cycling the SRPS, once, may clear the fault.

body:
ERROR: EM_DIAG_1WIRE_SEVERE_SRPS_FAULT
The 1-Wire Network indicates that the SRPS has a severe fault. The system can not clear this fault by itself. Manual SRPS recovery is necessary.
Extended error: This error indicates that the SRPS has a severe error such as an over-current or over-voltage that is way over the limit. The system can not reset this type of fault by itself. The SRPS must be power cycled. If the SRPS is currently faulted, the fault LED in its front panel will be lighted. Verify that the input power to the SRPS is correct. Run 1-wire diagnostics to see the current state of the individual SRPS fault and warning signals.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: Scan Room PS

Check if there are other VRF errors.

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2272600 - EM_RFHUB_BOARD_DETECT_FAILURE
body:
ERROR: EM_RFHUB_BOARD_DETECT_FAILURE
Hardware Failure. The RF Hub RFCB detected a board in the RF Hub is present via the backplane serial link, but did not detect the board present line.
Board: %b
Extended error: The RFCB did not detect a board present line for either a RFSB or MCDB, but the board is communicating to the RFCB across the backplane serial link.
Take out the RFCB and the board indicated and check for bent pins on the backplane. Try reseating both boards.
If reseating the boards does not work, replace the boards or the backplane.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: RF Hub Control Board, RF Hub Switch Board, RF Hub Multi-Coil Driver Board, RF Hub Backplane

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2272601 - EM_RFHUB_REMOTE_POWER_GOOD_FAILURE
body:
ERROR: EM_RFHUB_REMOTE_POWER_GOOD_FAILURE
Hardware Failure. The RF Hub RFCB detected a bad power detect line for a board in the RF Hub. The board was not detected, but the power detect line was good.
Board: %b
Extended error: The RFCB detected a digital power good signal from a board that is not present and not communicating on the backplane serial link.
Take out the RFCB and check for bent pins on the backplane. Try reseating the RFCB.
If reseating the board does not work, replace the board or the backplane.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: RF Hub Control Board, RF Hub Backplane

Board: %b
Extended error: The RFCB detected that the FPGA for a RFSB or MCDB was loaded successfully on a board that is not present and not commmunicating on the backplane serial link.
Take out the RFCB and check for bent pins on the backplane. Try reseating the RFCB.
If reseating the board does not work, replace the board or the backplane.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: RF Hub Control Board, RF Hub Backplane

title: 2273218 - EM_RFHUB_REROUTE_ONEWIRE_SEARCH_ERROR
body:
ERROR: EM_RFHUB_REROUTE_ONEWIRE_SEARCH_ERROR
The RF Hub detected an error searching for devices on the HART ID bus.
Error: %d
Extended error: Check the HART ID cable connected to the reroute box and the body coil. The one-wire search error will not impact ability to perform clinical scans.
Systems with an RFSBv or RFSB2 switch board in RF Hub Slots 1 (and 2, in case of 32 ch systems), will not have a Reroute Box. In such systems, this message is applicable to the devices which connected to the same one-wire bus. The Reroute box (if present), Preamp Combiner (if present), DTRSW (if present) and Body coil HART ID devices share a single one-wire bus controlled by the RF Hub. This error message is logged when the one-wire bus is shorted or when an invalid HART ID is received by the RF Hub. Check for bent pins at each connector in this path and test for one-wire bus short circuits within the cables. Refer to the system cabling diagrams. Run the RF Hub Board Level Diagnostic to retry the HART ID search.

title: 2273528 - EM_RFHUB_UNBLANK_CABLE_DISCONNECT
body:
ERROR: EM_RFHUB_UNBLANK_CABLE_DISCONNECT
The RF Hub detected that the unblank side of the unblank / inhibit cable is disconnected.
Extended error: Check that the Unblank / Inhibit cable on the RF Hub (RFCB J10) is connected to the PEN wall, and on the other side to the Exciter.
If both this message and the inhibit side message are seen, it is likely that the cable is disconnected at the RF Hub or PEN wall. This could also mean that the Unblank (RFCB J10) and Reroute Box / Table ID (RFCB J8) cables are swapped at the RF Hub.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: RF Hub Control Board, NB DTx Module

title: 2273546 - EM_RFHUB_RFCB_RRX_POWER_ERROR
body:
ERROR: EM_RFHUB_RFCB_RRX_POWER_ERROR
The RF Hub control board detected a RRx power error. Latched RRx fault bitmap: 0x%x
Extended error: The RF Hub detected RRx(s) that are reporting power errors. The power errors were latched in a bitmap of receivers reporting faults. The least significant bit corresponds to RRX-1. The RRx may need to be replaced. If all RRxs are reporting power faults, the TDM may need to be replaced. This error could also be caused by scan induced RF noise on the RRX to RF Hub cable, or a defective RF Hub control board or backplane
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: RRx Module, Transient Detection Module, RF Hub Control Board, RF Hub Backplane

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2273548 - EM_RFHUB_STARTUP_POWER_GOOD_PDB
body:
ERROR: EM_RFHUB_STARTUP_POWER_GOOD_PDB
RF Hub Hardware Failure. The RF Hub RFCB read from the PDB that analog power is good before power is enabled. TPS reset and scanning will fail until this is fixed.
Common: %s
RFCB: %s%s
MCDB: %s%s
RFSB: %s
Extended error: The RFCB only turns on analog power to the PDB after startup checks are run. If analog power is detected before this, it means that either the RFCB, PDB, or Backplane is faulty.
Remove the RFCB and PDB and check for bent pins.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: RF Hub Control Board, RF Hub Power Distribution Board, RF Hub Backplane

Board: %b
Power: %s%s%s%s%s
Extended error: The RFCB only turns on analog power to the PDB after startup checks are run. If analog power is detected before this, it means that either the RFCB, PDB, RFSB, MCDB, or Backplane is faulty.
Remove the RFCB, PDB, and the board indicated, and check for bent pins.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: RF Hub Control Board, RF Hub Power Distribution Board, RF Hub Switch Board, RF Hub Multi-Coil Driver Board, RF Hub Backplane

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2273550 - EM_RFHUB_POWER_BAD_PDB
body:

Common: %s
RFCB: %s%s
MCDB: %s%s
RFSB: %s
Extended error: Power good signals from the PDB to the RFCB indicated the power is bad for the supplies in the error message.
Check for SRPS power errors. If the SRPS is supplying power correctly, and this issue keeps occuring, it could indicate a bad RFCB, PDB, or RF Hub backplane.
Remove the RFCB and PDB and check for bent pins on the backplane.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: Scan Room PS, RF Hub Control Board, RF Hub Power Distribution Board

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2274013 - EM_RFHUB_MC_SHORT_UNUSED_ADC
body:
ERROR: EM_RFHUB_MC_SHORT_UNUSED_ADC
Unused Channel Fault - Short Circuit A multicoil bias fault was detected. Reseat all coils and check coil connections.
Connector: %b Channels faulted: 0x%lx
First channel: %ld of %ld, counting from 1
Fault value: %ld mV, Channel: %d
Extended error: A short circuit was detected by the RF Hub on a channel that is not known to be connected a coil. This could indicate a coil is plugged in that is not being read by coil ID.
Run the Multicoil Bias Diagnostic or Coil Datapath Diagnostic to troubleshoot.
Explanation of fields:
Connector - The coil connector the fault was detected on. Channels faulted - This is a hexadecimal bit map of all the faulted channels. For example, 0x3 means faults on channels 1 and 2. 0x80000000 means channel 32. First channel - The first channel that faulted, and the number of channels on the connector. Fault value - The voltage seen when the fault was detected, on the channel.

title: 2274052 - EM_RFHUB_MC_TOLERANCE
body:
ERROR: EM_RFHUB_MC_TOLERANCE
Multicoil Bias Drive Fault The RF Hub detected that the multicoil bias voltage was not driven correctly.
Connector: %b Fault bitmap: 0x%lx, Used bitmap: 0x%lx
First channel: %ld of %ld
Driven: %ld mV, Read: %ld mV
Extended error: A bias drive fault was detected by the RF Hub. This happens when the RF Hub tries to drive a multicoil bias voltage, but detects that the voltage driven is outside of the expected range.
Ignore this error if there are also RF Hub power failures reported. If no power failures are reported, this is likely a faulty RF Hub RFCB or MCDB.
Run the Multicoil Bias Diagnostic or Coil Datapath Diagnostic to troubleshoot.
Explanation of fields:
Connector - The coil connector the fault was detected on. Fault bitmap - This is a hexadecimal bit map of all the faulted channels. For example, 0x3 means faults on channels 1 and 2. 0x80000000 means channel 32. Used bitmap - This is a hexadecimal bit map of the channels on this connector that are known to be connected to a coil. First channel - The first channel that faulted, and the number of channels on the connector. Driven - The voltage programmed. Read - The voltage read back that is outside of the expected range.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: RF Hub Control Board, RF Hub Multi-Coil Driver Board

Port: %b
Connector Fault Voltage: %d mV
Expected Voltage Range: %d mV - %d mV

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2274528 - EM_CFB_DIAG_LOOPBACK_FAILED
body:
ERROR: EM_CFB_DIAG_LOOPBACK_FAILED
CFB Diagnostic Error. Loopback test of channel %d on the CFB failed
Extended error: The CAN Fiber Optic Board (CFB) has 6 fiber optic channels for communication in and out of the scan room. This diagnostic requires that the channel on the CFB have a fiber optic loopback connector tool installed. If the connector was installed on the correct channel for the test, it likely means that the CFB fiber optic transmitter/receiver is bad or the fiber optic loopback connector is defective. Channel 1 is the SRI CANopen fiber optic connection Channel 2 is the RF Hub CANopen fiber optic connections Channel 3 is the PAC fiber optic pass through (in normal operation this passes the signal from channel 4) Channel 4 is the STIF(or PSE) fiber optic pass through (in normal operation this passes the signal from channel 3) Channel 5 is unused Channel 6 is unused
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: CAN Fiber Board

ERROR: EM_RF_HUB_DIAG_RRX_LOOPBACK_CMD_ERROR
The IRF/RRX could not place the RF Hub CAN Fibers into loopback mode.
Extended error: RRX control of the RF Hub CAN fiber loopback mode failed, but the loopback test will continue in case the fiber connections on the CFB are jumpered. If the fiber connections are not jumpered, check the RRX to RF Hub cables that carry the RF Hub remote command signals and run the RRX to RF Hub Datapath Diagnostic. TPS reset might also help.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: RRx Module, Dual Fiber Cable, IRF Board

title: 2274814 - EM_RF_HUB_DIAG_CFB_LOOPBACK_FAILED

The CFB -> RF Hub loopback test failed
Extended error: The CAN Fiber Board to RF Hub loopback test failed. Check the fiber connections at the CAN Fiber Board and RF Hub. Check the CAN copper connection at the CFB. Check the RRX to RF Hub cables; these carry the RF Hub remote command signals. Run the RRX to RF Hub Datapath Diagnostic. TPS reset might also help.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: Dual Fiber Cable, RF Hub Backplane, RF Hub Control Board, CAN Fiber Board, RRx Module

result= %d
Extended error: The CAN Fiber Board could not execute the loopback test for the RF Hub fiber channel. This error does not indicate a problem with the RF Hub or the fibers. Run CAN Fiber Board diagnostics to isolate the problem.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: CAN Fiber Board

Possible cause(s), most to least probable: Dual Fiber Cable, CAN Fiber Board

Possible cause(s), most to least probable: RRx Module, Dual Fiber Cable, IRF Board

Bad electrical table dock. Undock and try again.
Extended error: The diagnostic detected a problem with the electrical table dock. One or more of the coil port connectors in the table was not detected. This can occur if the electrical dock pedal was not fully depressed. Undock the table and attempt to redock it. Check the coil port cable connections at the RF Hub control board. Then re-run the diagnostic. If the problem persists, run the Coil Datapath Diagnostic that utilizes the MCRv tool to isolate the cause.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: RF Hub Control Board

doc_title: GE MR Error Message Tool (GE System Log extended errors)
title: 2274827 - EM_RF_HUB_DIAG_IRFLINK_BAD
body:
ERROR: EM_RF_HUB_DIAG_IRFLINK_BAD
One or more RRX is reporting a bad IRF DVMR link connection. Failed RRX bitmap: 0x%x
Extended error: The RF Hub detected RRx(s) that are reporting IRF DVMR Link errors. The errors were latched in a bitmap of receivers reporting faults. The least significant bit corresponds to RRX-1. If all RRxs are reporting IRF DVMR Link faults, the fibers may be bad or the link may be disconnected. Check for other error messages regarding link failures. If only some of the RRxs are reporting IRF Link faults, the RRX may need to be replaced. Run the RRX diagnostics to troubleshoot. This error could also be caused by scan induced RF noise on the RRX to RF Hub cable, or a defective RF Hub control board or backplane. Run the RF Hub - Receiver Datapath Diagnostic to troubleshoot.
Possible cause(s), most to least probable: IRF Board, Dual Fiber Cable, RRx Module, RF Hub Backplane, RF Hub Control Board

title: 2274906 - EM_RF_HUB_DIAG_MCRV_BIAS_CONNA_DC_FAULTS
body:

Connector A bias faults were detected exclusively on the DC bias path.
Extended error: The MCRv tool places a diode-resistive load on the DC bias path on the 37-Pin control cable for Connector A. The load is reversed biased and appears as an open circuit for positive bias currents and voltages, and as a resistive load for negative bias currents and voltages. This error message indicates that only the negative current/voltage bias checks failed. Check the Connector A DC bias path from the RFCB J6, through the cable track, to Connector A on the LPCA.

The load is reversed biased and appears as an open circuit for negative bias currents and voltages, and as a resistive load for positive bias currents and voltages. This error message indicates that only the positive current/voltage bias checks failed. Check the Connector A RF bias path from the RF Switchboard, through the reroute box, and the cable track, to Connector A on the LPCA.
